paragraphs: Three days passed in the blink of an eye. News of a perfect pill appearing in Caprath spread like wildfire, and people were in an uproar.
Everyone wanted to get their hands on the pill, while alchemists were desperate to uncover the identity of its mysterious creator.
Crowds began storming the Silver Leaf Auction House. The closest anyone had come to this elusive alchemist, however, was Manager Alina.

Speaking of Alina, after it was revealed that she had advanced to become a Root Grandmaster—a Level 4 one at that—her status soared. Her importance to the Silver Leaf Auction House skyrocketed, making her their most prized asset.
Everyone sought to earn her favor, while the leader of the auction house hoped to capitalize on her miraculous transformation by using her as a symbol of excellence for their establishment.
The Silver Leaf Auction House had become a must-visit destination thanks to Kent’s miraculous pills.
Alina had given only four pills out of the hundreds she had received from Kent to the owner of the Silver Leaf Auction house.
Although not much, that was more than enough to secure her spot as the auctioneer for the upcoming annual auction in two months.
Naturally, they planned to auction these Tier 0 pills soon. Although it might seem like a rash decision, everyone was eager to verify whether the pills were truly as perfect as rumored.
Alina told the owner she could get more pills from the alchemist. So the leader wasn’t worried about making a fool of herself.
Craving fame and publicity, the auction house announced they would auction three Tier 0 pills in a week, and excitement swept through the entire city and beyond.
Such was the power and allure of a perfect pill.
But while one establishment was soaring, another was struggling. Somewhere in the city—specifically in the Ashland family—a lady dressed in dark clothing sat with a frown on her face.
Well, to be precise, she was wearing a mask with a frown painted on it.
It seemed that nothing could excite her, as she always wore a frown, no matter the situation.
Perhaps she was simply weary of life and used the frown to convey that. In some ways, that feels deeply unsettling.
But she wore it well. But unlike her emotions, which were expressed through her mask, the others around her weren’t as composed.
Dave Ashland and Daisy Ashland lay sprawled on the floor, their faces drained of all color. In the presence of a peak Root Sage, resistance is futile.
Of course, it was their own stupidity that brought them to this point. They had failed to meet expectations, and now they were suffering the consequences.
Nearby, Vida, Rita, and Yin Ashland lay unconscious on the floor. Well, Vida was more than unconscious—she was dead.
The whole family was utterly dysfunctional.

"So, let me get this straight," the lady said, her voice devoid of any warmth. "You’re telling me that the Spirit Root I intended to claim for your daughter, so I can add another powerhouse to my Devil Spirit Church—has somehow slipped through your fingers.
"And instead of taking decisive action to secure her through other means, you thought it best to wait for me to step in and clean up your mess? Is that what you’re saying?"
Her tone was sharp, almost venomous.

Dave Ashland turned an even ghastlier shade of pale—if that was even possible. Already pale, his complexion seemed to drain further, leaving him a ghostly shell. It was almost comical if it weren’t so tragic.
Daisy wasn’t doing much better.
"My lady, please try to understand. The Alderford family is now under the protection of a Root Sage; we don’t have the strength to oppose her," Daisy managed to say between short, strained breaths.
The oppressive aura suffocating them was far too overwhelming. Despite both being Peak Root Saints, they were utterly powerless under the crushing might of a Peak Root Sage’s aura.
It was like an ant trying to lift a celestial boulder with a single arm.
"I see. So, there’s a situation like that. Why didn’t you start with that?" the lady said, her tone sharp as she finally withdrew her suffocating aura.
Daisy and Dave collapsed to the floor, gasping for air, their bodies trembling from the release of pressure.
"Tell me about this Root Sage protecting them," she demanded coldly.

Daisy wasted no time. "She’s one of the Masters at the Sword Gate of the Divine Palace Sect—Sword Saintess Selene. She recently took on a disciple, and that disciple happens to be the alchemist who cured the young miss of the Alderford family.

"Oddly enough, the young miss has decided to become his woman, and ever since, Sword Saintess Selene has been staying with them. She’s been living there for the past week, making it impossible for us to take any action against them."

"I see. That’s... actually troublesome," the lady said, a faint flicker of annoyance crossing her voice. "I’ve fought that woman before. While she wouldn’t be able to kill me outright, I also don’t think I can easily deal with her."
"But that doesn’t mean we’re not going to try," the Dark Lady said, her voice unwavering.
"What do you require of us, Lady Dark?" Daisy asked, her tone as respectful as she could muster.
"It’s very simple," the Dark Lady replied. "Since she has taken a disciple, it’s only a matter of time before they return to the sect, correct? We’ll ambush them on the way and take what we need.
"However, be prepared to sacrifice a few soldiers. Deploy scouts to monitor their movements and report back to me. The moment they head for the sect, inform me immediately."
As soon as the words left her mouth, the Dark Lady disappeared from the room, her presence vanishing as if she had never been there.
Dave and Daisy breathed heavy sighs of relief, their bodies sagging as the oppressive tension lifted.
"That was harder than I expected," Dave Ashland said, his face returning to its natural color.
"Harder than expected? We were this close to dying," Daisy said with a frown.

"We didn’t, which means our plan has started to take shape. If we’re lucky, she will be killed, and her hold on us will be lifted. Then we can start our next plan to gain the power we need," Dave said.

"That is true, but we don’t know what the Devil Spirit Church wants to do in this kingdom, so we can only hope that once we gain their favor, they won’t stab us in the back," Daisy said, looking somewhat excited.

"They won’t. Since we won’t be getting the spirit root for our daughter and then selling her to the Devil Spirit Church is now meaningless. We can only sell the Atomic Divine Body. That said, my men retrieved her a day ago and have now locked her inside the Makosa Prison," Dave replied.

Craving fame and publicity, the auction house announced they would auction three Tier 0 pills in a week, and excitement swept through the entire city and beyond.
Such was the power and allure of a perfect pill.
But while one establishment was soaring, another was struggling.
Somewhere in the city—specifically in the Ashland family—a lady dressed in dark clothing sat with a frown on her face.
Well, to be precise, she was wearing a mask with a frown painted on it.
It seemed that nothing could excite her, as she always wore a frown, no matter the situation.
Perhaps she was simply weary of life and used the frown to convey that.
In some ways, that feels deeply unsettling.
But she wore it well.
But unlike her emotions, which were expressed through her mask, the others around her weren’t as composed.
Dave Ashland and Daisy Ashland lay sprawled on the floor, their faces drained of all color.
In the presence of a peak Root Sage, resistance is futile.
Of course, it was their own stupidity that brought them to this point.
They had failed to meet expectations, and now they were suffering the consequences.
Nearby, Vida, Rita, and Yin Ashland lay unconscious on the floor.
Well, Vida was more than unconscious—she was dead.
The whole family was utterly dysfunctional.
"So, let me get this straight," the lady said, her voice devoid of any warmth.
"You’re telling me that the Spirit Root I intended to claim for your daughter, so I can add another powerhouse to my Devil Spirit Church—has somehow slipped through your fingers.
"And instead of taking decisive action to secure her through other means, you thought it best to wait for me to step in and clean up your mess?
Is that what you’re saying?"
Her tone was sharp, almost venomous.
Dave Ashland turned an even ghastlier shade of pale—if that was even possible.
Already pale, his complexion seemed to drain further, leaving him a ghostly shell.
It was almost comical if it weren’t so tragic.
Daisy wasn’t doing much better.
"My lady, please try to understand.
The Alderford family is now under the protection of a Root Sage; we don’t have the strength to oppose her," Daisy managed to say between short, strained breaths.
The oppressive aura suffocating them was far too overwhelming.
Despite both being Peak Root Saints, they were utterly powerless under the crushing might of a Peak Root Sage’s aura.
It was like an ant trying to lift a celestial boulder with a single arm.
"I see.
So, there’s a situation like that.
Why didn’t you start with that?" the lady said, her tone sharp as she finally withdrew her suffocating aura.
Daisy and Dave collapsed to the floor, gasping for air, their bodies trembling from the release of pressure.
"Tell me about this Root Sage protecting them," she demanded coldly.
Daisy wasted no time.
"She’s one of the Masters at the Sword Gate of the Divine Palace Sect—Sword Saintess Selene.
She recently took on a disciple, and that disciple happens to be the alchemist who cured the young miss of the Alderford family.
"Oddly enough, the young miss has decided to become his woman, and ever since, Sword Saintess Selene has been staying with them.
She’s been living there for the past week, making it impossible for us to take any action against them."
"I see.
That’s... actually troublesome," the lady said, a faint flicker of annoyance crossing her voice.
"I’ve fought that woman before.
While she wouldn’t be able to kill me outright, I also don’t think I can easily deal with her."
"But that doesn’t mean we’re not going to try," the Dark Lady said, her voice unwavering.
"What do you require of us, Lady Dark?" Daisy asked, her tone as respectful as she could muster.
"It’s very simple," the Dark Lady replied.
"Since she has taken a disciple, it’s only a matter of time before they return to the sect, correct?
We’ll ambush them on the way and take what we need.
"However, be prepared to sacrifice a few soldiers.
Deploy scouts to monitor their movements and report back to me.
The moment they head for the sect, inform me immediately."
As soon as the words left her mouth, the Dark Lady disappeared from the room, her presence vanishing as if she had never been there.
Dave and Daisy breathed heavy sighs of relief, their bodies sagging as the oppressive tension lifted.
"That was harder than I expected," Dave Ashland said, his face returning to its natural color.
"Harder than expected?
We were this close to dying," Daisy said with a frown.
"We didn’t, which means our plan has started to take shape.
If we’re lucky, she will be killed, and her hold on us will be lifted.
Then we can start our next plan to gain the power we need," Dave said.

"That is true, but we don’t know what the Devil Spirit Church wants to do in this kingdom, so we can only hope that once we gain their favor, they won’t stab us in the back," Daisy said, looking somewhat excited.
"They won’t.
Since we won’t be getting the spirit root for our daughter and then selling her to the Devil Spirit Church is now meaningless.
We can only sell the Atomic Divine Body.
That said, my men retrieved her a day ago and have now locked her inside the Makosa Prison," Dave replied.
"Good.
Once the Dark Lady is dead, we will make our stand.
Soon, the entire kingdom will be ours to rule," Daisy said before jumping on Dave.
Soon, her moans filled the hall, while her sisters remained passed out, one of them dead.
Clearly, they may appear weak to many, but their schemes are already taking shape.

chapters.title: Chapter 66: Looking for Li Hua (1)
paragraphs: Immediately after leaving the mansion, Kent used his teleportation skills to travel several times, and soon, he was in the city.
He could now teleport 2 kilometers at a time, so it only took a few teleportations to enter the city. But then his problem began.

He didn’t know where to go next. The last time he and Unity had been there, it was to buy ingredients for pills. They had only spent a few hours roaming around, so he knew little about the city beyond the herb store and the auction house.
But today, he wasn’t there for herbs or to visit the auction house. He wanted to explore the city and see what it had to offer.
Of course, he didn’t want to wander aimlessly. But with no guidance available, he could only stroll around, hoping to stumble upon something interesting.
It didn’t take long before he started seeing things he liked. He first went to a restaurant, where he spent a few spirit stones devouring some of their finest meals.
Compared to the meals he’d had back on Earth, these were far more delicious and brimming with energy.

Naturally, in this world of cultivation, almost everything that can be eaten contains spiritual energy. This was especially true for the meats, which came from spirit beasts. The energy in them was highly potent. Kent ate his fill before leaving.

He began moving around, attracting attention as he moved. Of course, he didn’t mind. Naturally, he rejected all the proposals he received along the way. Most of the ladies wanted to pay him for a night with them, but he politely declined.
He wasn’t there as a gigolo.
Five hours later, Kent started fighting off the urge to enter a brothel, as moving around alone was much more boring than he had anticipated.
He just wanted to enter and see for himself what it was made of. Of course, he didn’t want to, but with nothing else of interest, he began to consider it.
However, just as his desires were starting to take over, a certain small human came to mind.
"Good idea. If I find that tiny human, she would certainly know some amazing places I can explore," Kent muttered before moving away.
Soon, he was in front of Li Hua’s cake shop. However, just like four days ago, it was closed. This time, though, he asked the store next door.
"Excuse me, miss. Do you know why this store is closed?" Kent asked.
"Sorry, young man, but I don’t know. You might want to ask the next store; maybe they would know something," the store lady politely replied.
"Alright, thanks." Kent moved to the next store.
"Please, do you know why Li Hua has closed the store?" This time, he asked in a tone that showed he was familiar with the tiny human.
"Well, they closed down the store a few days ago after making a big sale, and since then, they haven’t opened up," the store lady answered, making Kent frown slightly.
"Would this happen to be four days ago?" he asked.

"Yes. They closed the shop about four days ago and haven’t come to work since. It isn’t like them. They used to be the first to open shop on this side of town, so it was rather shocking when they stopped coming around."
"I see. Please, do you know where they stay?" Kent asked. He immediately suspected it had something to do with the spirit stones he gave the tiny human, so he wanted to get to the root of it.
Since he was bored anyway, looking for the small human and her grandma was something he could do to pass the time.
A few minutes later, he left and headed to the northern part of the city. Even after teleporting a couple of times, it took him an hour to get there.

Li Hua and her grandma live in a small village-like part of the city called Brown Tree. The name is literal, as when Kent approached the northern part of the city, a large brown tree could be seen in the distance.
It has been there for ages, hence the moniker given to the village. Kent quickly made his way in the direction the storewoman had given him.
A few minutes later, a small house with a baking furnace in the center appeared in front of him. Clearly, this was Li Hua’s home. They were bakers, after all, hence the furnace.
"This must be it," Kent said, walking toward the house.
Kent didn’t know why, but he felt scared of what he might find out. In fact, despite not knowing the small human that much, he still was scared as to what he might discover.
The last time he met Li Hua, she had only wanted to sell him banana cakes for two copper coins. However, because he didn’t have copper coins with him, he gave her spirit stones instead.
This meant that while he didn’t care, it was a big deal for Li Hua and those who had witnessed their transaction.
Right now, he felt bad about what might have happened to them. If something had happened to her because he decided to show off his wealth, he would feel guilty about it.
The moment he approached the door, Kent could see it was open. He wasted no time and entered, hoping the small human or her grandma would be inside. However, to his disappointment, he found nothing.
He began looking around the room but could only see a small bed, clearly meant for Li Hua.
Nothing was out of place, but Kent didn’t see it that way. He activated his Appraiser’s Eye skill and began inspecting the house with his divine sense.
Shortly after, he noticed that some things were indeed out of place in the other room. A lamp was knocked down, and the bed seemed to have been moved.

Kent quickly entered that room and moved the bed further. Beneath it, he found a small compartment that had been opened. However, it was empty. Clearly, whatever had been inside was taken, and the compartment had not been properly closed.
"This is not looking good," he muttered.
"Tower, do you have any insight as to what might have happened here?" Kent asked, desperate.
[No, Master, but they seem to have some neighbors. You might want to ask them,] the Tower suggested.
Kent nodded. "How foolish of me. However, what is your take on this room?" he still asked.
[Clearly, it has been tampered with. However, from the look of things, it was done by someone who knew what they were doing.]
"You think Li Hua or her grandma did this?" Kent asked.
[It seems so. If it had been an intruder, the room would have been much messier than this. But that is just my assumption. You would have to ask the neighbors for more information.]
Kent nodded, and after spending a few more minutes looking around the house, he went out to ask around.
Of course, he didn’t take long to spot a young man snooping around Li Hua’s house.
The man ran as soon as he saw Kent come out of the house, but before he could take three steps, Kent used his [Teleport] skill and appeared before him.

If it had been an intruder, the room would have been much messier than this.
But that is just my assumption.
You would have to ask the neighbors for more information.]
Kent nodded, and after spending a few more minutes looking around the house, he went out to ask around.
Of course, he didn’t take long to spot a young man snooping around Li Hua’s house.
The man ran as soon as he saw Kent come out of the house, but before he could take three steps, Kent used his [Teleport] skill and appeared before him.

chapters.title: Chapter 67: Looking for Li Hua (2)
paragraphs: Kent immediately appeared in front of the young man, blocking his path. The young man froze, his eyes wide with panic, and stumbled back a step.
He was sneaking around, after all, so getting caught completely off-guard startled him. Kent had used the teleport skill to appear before him, making his sudden presence even more alarming.
"Hey, easy there," Kent said, holding up his hands in a calming gesture. "I don’t mean you any harm, just wanna talk."
The young man hesitated, looking for an escape route. But then his brain did some quick calculations, and he decided to calm down and listen to the man.
After all, he had been 300 meters away, yet this man appeared before him as if they’d been standing face to face. There was no escaping him even if he gave it his all.
"I mean it," Kent continued. "I just want to talk. Look, I’m looking for Li Hua and her grandma. You know them, right?"
"And what is your name, by the way?" Kent asked, making sure to ease the tension.
"Chen," the young man replied, his breathing starting to even out.
"Okay, Chen. Can you tell me when you last saw Li Hua or her grandma?" Kent asked.
"Uh, it was two days ago," Chen said, rubbing the back of his neck. "I saw Li Hua early in the morning. But that was all for that day."
’Hmm, looks like she was alright until two days ago,’ Kent thought, his mood lifting a bit.
"Okay. Did she seem worried when you saw her two days ago?" Kent asked again.

"Not that I can think of. However, I did hear something funny during the night. But since it wasn’t any of my business, I never bothered to check. Well, I checked today since Li Hua didn’t bring cake."
"Something funny? Care to elaborate?"
"Yes. I heard some dragging, like something—furniture being dragged across the floor."
Kent’s expression turned serious as he leaned in slightly. "Dragging furniture? Did you hear voices or anything else unusual?"

Chen nodded hesitantly. "Not really voices, just the sound of things moving around. It was late, and I figured it was just them shifting stuff in the house. They bake a lot; maybe they were moving supplies or something."
"I see," Kent muttered.
’It looks like the bed that was dragged was what he was talking about,’ Kent thought, his expression shifting slightly. This situation was getting more confusing by the minute.

"Do you know where Li Hua and her grandma might go if they were in trouble? Or maybe a place they’d visit to relax? Did Li Hua ever mention anything like that?" Kent asked, keeping his tone calm but focused.
Chen furrowed his brow, clearly trying to recall. After a moment, he nodded.

"Li Hua did mention a shed in the woods once. She said she and her grandma used to go there to relax sometimes. It’s a little far from her but just a short walk past the river on the village’s outskirts."
Kent’s eyes lit up with a mix of hope and determination. "A shed in the woods... That’s good to know. Thanks, Chen. You’ve been really helpful."
Chen shrugged. "I just hope they’re okay. Li Hua’s a good person, and her grandma... well, she can be a little strict, but she means well."
"I’ll find them," Kent said firmly. He retrieved a pouch and gave it to Chen.
Before he could open it, Kent was already several kilometers away. Chen finally opened the pouch, and his eyes widened. Just like that, Kent had changed his life, gifting him 20,000 spirit stones.
After teleporting dozens of times, Kent stopped and began walking instead. Soon, he arrived at the river Chen had mentioned.
He crossed it swiftly and continued toward the shed Chen had described. Of course, since he didn’t know the exact location, he relied on his divine sense, scanning the 12-kilometer radius thoroughly.
He wasn’t in a rush, so even after two hours, he had only covered a few miles into the woods. Along the way, he noticed several spirit beasts between Tier 1 and Tier 3 in the area.
[A/N: Spirit Beasts share the same cultivation base as humans, but their levels are measured in Tiers. Tier 1 corresponds to Root Awakening...and the progression follows a similar pattern.]
They posed no real challenge to him, so Kent didn’t pay them much attention. Of course, a few dared to confront him, only to fall swiftly under his sword.
Five hours later, he still hadn’t found the shed, and the weather began to shift. The night was approaching, but Kent didn’t care.
An hour later, his senses detected a small shed a few kilometers to the east. Without hesitation, he teleported, appearing at the location within seconds.
It was a small woodshed. Everything was made of wood, but from the look of it, the wood wasn’t ordinary. Even after years, it still looked sturdy and showed no signs of losing its quality.
However, the door was kicked in and broken halfway. Kent’s senses immediately spread out, but he didn’t detect anything. This made him quickly rush in to see what was wrong.
The moment he walked through the door. However, an attack appeared right in front of him. It was so sudden that as soon as he creaked open the broken door, the attack reached him.
The next second, Kent was 2 km away from the house.
He had used [Teleport] at the last moment to escape. But he quickly made his way back to the shed again.

This time, however, he didn’t rush in. Instead, he decided to speak first. The fact that he wasn’t able to sense anyone, yet someone was inside the small house, made him fear for his life. However, he wasn’t about to leave—not just yet.
Of course, before saying anything, he had to ask the tower first.
<Tower, do you sense anyone inside?> Kent asked.
[Yes, master. A powerful soul cultivator is inside, but they are near death.]
<Near death.> Kent’s heartbeat slowed for a moment. Though he didn’t know Li Hua that well, he just couldn’t bear the thought of the little human dying—or worse, becoming someone’s puppet forever.

"Hello there. My name is Kent. I’m somewhat of a friend to the small little human called Li Hua. Well, we’re not exactly close, but I bought banana cakes from her and might have put a target on her back when I gave her spirit stones instead of copper coins.
"If you know something, please tell me. I have reasons to believe her life might be in danger because of my reckless actions, and I just want to help," Kent said, walking slowly toward the door.

He didn’t know who was inside or why he couldn’t sense them. However, he wasn’t about to find out the hard way. This situation could turn dangerous quickly, and he wasn’t willing to take unnecessary risks.
Luckily for him, a voice came from the small house the next moment.
"Are you the handsome big brother who gave her the spirit stones?" the voice asked, sounding curious.
’Handsome big brother?’ Kent clicked his tongue but decided to respond.
"Yes, I am the handsome big brother." It sounded ridiculous, but he had to say it.
A few seconds later, the door creaked open wide.
"Enter..."

chapters.title: Chapter 68: Janice, Li Hua’s Beast Guardian
paragraphs: Kent walked through the door the next second. As soon as he entered the small house, he saw an old lady sitting in a pool of blood, her face deathly pale.
Kent quickly moved toward her, but a gentle force stopped him before he could get much closer.
"No need. I am beyond saving, young man," the old lady said weakly.

Kent’s eyes scanned the room, noticing signs of a struggle and several bloodstains scattered around. To his right lay a body—a lifeless figure clad in a black cloak. A dagger was sheathed at the figure’s leg and waist.
"What happened here?" Kent asked, his voice edged with concern. He added, "Let me look at your wound. I am an Alchemist, maybe I can help."
The old lady shook her head slowly. "It’s of no use. I am long dead. You cannot save me."
Kent stared at her with a perplexed expression. The woman was sitting right in front of him, yet she claimed she was already dead.
It made no sense—at least, not until the tower, having had a few seconds to analyze the situation, provided clarity.

[Master, that is not a human. From her blood, she appears to be a spirit beast, specifically a Golden Tail Soul Fox. They are a race of spirit beasts renowned for their powerful souls and strong mental strength. If I am not mistaken, she is using a technique called Afterdeath Incarnation to hold her soul for some time.]
<There’s something like that?> Kent’s eyes widened as he absorbed this new piece of knowledge.
"Are you really the big brother who gave her the spirit stones?" the old lady asked, her voice barely audible.
"Yes. And I’m sorry if it has caused her any trouble. I never intended for that," Kent apologized earnestly.
"Nothing is your fault, young man. Because of you, we even had a shot at escaping this time," the old lady said, a faint smile tugging at her lips.
"Escaping this time?" Kent raised an eyebrow, his curiosity piqued.

"You seem like a perceptive young man, so I know you know Li Hua is no ordinary human. That aside, she is indeed not a normal human. She was born with a rare type of Heavenly Body Constitution; because of this, her life was in constant danger.

"We have to keep moving now and then just to escape those who mean her harm. Finally, we managed to come here, and for the past 11 years, we have had peace until a few days ago when danger found us again.

"We managed to escape, and thanks to your spirit stones, we were going to disappear, which could have helped us live for a few more years until Li Hua could start to cultivate. Once she did, nobody would have been able to find her again.
"Yet, I underestimated the danger this time, and, well, as you can see, I am dead, and Li Hua has been taken away," the old lady said with a painful expression.
Kent immediately knew where she was going with everything, so he didn’t let her finish.
"I want to help. Please tell me where they have taken Li Hua, and I promise I will bring her back," Kent said with a determined expression.
The old lady looked at him for a moment. Within that moment, Kent felt a gentle yet potent energy wash over him like it was probing him.

A few seconds later, the lady sighed. "You look capable, but you’re still too weak to protect her. However, I don’t have much time, and it isn’t like there’s much else I can do. So, I will have to trust you.
That being said, I must warn you that the moment you take the next step, your life will become much more chaotic since Li Hua is a rather unique human.
Are you willing?" she asked.

So far, the conversation had been cryptic and strange. Kent knew the old lady was Li Hua’s grandmother. However, knowing that she wasn’t human left him rather taken aback. Then again, if she isn’t human, why does she look like one?
That answer came faster than he had expected. Vexthra, his first wife—the goddess—wasn’t human, yet she looked human. This meant the lady before him had simply disguised herself as one.
Another question quickly arose: If she isn’t human, why is she with Li Hua, acting like some kind of guardian? That answer came the next moment.
"I don’t have much time, but since Li Hua seems to think you’re a good person, even in those few seconds she had known you, I will have to trust you," she said.

The next second, the lady transformed, revealing her true form—a cute-looking white fox adorned with intricate golden patterns tracing across her body. Her golden eyes shimmered with a soft, ethereal glow, and her single tail radiated a gentle brilliance.

"My name is Janice. I am a Golden Tail Soul Fox. For the past 13 years, I was tasked by Li Hua’s father to guard his daughter with my life. Let’s just say...I failed," she said, her voice trembling with weakness.
"This is why, even though I don’t know you and you have no obligation to help me...I would still like to beg you to look after Li Hua," Janice continued, her tone laced with desperation.
"You want me to become her guardian?" Kent asked, his expression serious.

"Yes. I want you to protect her until she is able to start cultivating and defending herself," Janice replied hastily. Her presence began to dim, her form fading as she struggled to hold onto her soul.
"Okay. I’m willing," Kent responded without hesitation.
"Thank you," Janice said, a faint smile crossing her face. A small stone emerged from her body and floated toward Kent, who caught it deftly.
<What is this?> Kent asked internally.
[It’s a guardian stone. If you fuse with it, you will form a link with the one you are meant to protect. This link allows you to sense them within a certain radius,] the Tower explained.
<I see,> Kent thought.

"That is a guardian stone," Janice said aloud. "Fusing with it will connect you to Li Hua. There isn’t much time left, so please do it before I cease to exist entirely," she pleaded, her voice faint and strained.
Kent nodded, channeling his energy into the stone. As he did, a series of messages began to appear before him.
[You have fused with a Guardian Stone. +100 added to your spiritual strength permanently.]
[Requirement met... Guardian Tower has been unlocked. You must become a Root Grandmaster to awaken it fully.]
[You have added the human named Li Hua to your Guardian Tower.]
[Because this is your first time becoming a Guardian, the skill named [Guardians Protect] has been unlocked.]
[Guardians Protect]
Grade: Divine
Rank: SSS
-- You can sense those under your protection from 2 miles away. This will continue to increase as your soul grows.
-- Whenever someone under your protection is harmed, you will get a 500% boost to all your attributes for 10 minutes.
> Side Effect: Extreme anger and bloodlust.
-- All those under your protection will inherit a part of your strength when in a life-and-death situation.
> Note: You will not get weakened in any way.
-- You will gain a part of the spiritual qi from those under your protection while they are cultivating.
-- Once every day, you can use the skill [Guardians Fury] to protect those linked to you. This skill will give you a 2,000% boost in all your attributes.
’Damn.’

chapters.title: Chapter 69: Soul Cultivation
paragraphs: Kent was a little startled by the turn of events. Things were moving faster than he could comprehend, yet he could tell he had unlocked another strength.
’A Guardian Tower, huh,’ Kent thought, feeling a flicker of happiness. But with Li Hua still missing, he forced himself to stay calm and focus on what he was there to do.
"I am done," Kent said as the Guardian Stone vanished to who knows where. Janice didn’t seem to care about that. Her form was now flickering in and out of existence.
Her life force had long departed the waking world. Only an afterimage of her lifeforce, preserved in soul form, remained.
"Good. Since I failed my mission to protect the young miss, I will ensure you have the power to save her. Whether or not you can make it, your strength will depend on your destiny.
Give me your hand."
Kent quickly obeyed and extended his hand.
"When you find the young miss, tell her I’m sorry. Tell her to forgive me for letting her down."
As soon as Janice uttered those words, she dissolved into a golden smoke that entered his hand.
Kent was startled for a moment, but then a new set of messages began to appear.
[You have absorbed a soul relic. Name: Golden Tail Soul Fox Soul Shard.]
[Requirement met... Soul Tower awakening.]
[You have unlocked the Soul Tower. You must become a Root Grandmaster to awaken it fully.]
[Your Chaos Dragon bloodline is reacting to the soul shard... Your Chaos Dragon bloodline has merged with the soul shard.]
[Attempting to awaken a new class...]
[Congratulations, you have awakened a new class.]
[Class Name: Soul Cultivator (Spirit Master)]
[Level: Tier 1]
-- You now can practice soul cultivation.
-- You have gained the power to communicate with and control spirit entities such as Beasts, Weapons, and Spirits.
-- You can enhance your physical and spiritual abilities by refining your soul energy.
-- You can learn and practice unique soul-based techniques and combat arts.
[You have unlocked a new Soul skill: Soul Absorb.]
[Skill Name: Soul Absorb]
[Grade: Divine]
[Rank: SSS]
-- Absorb the soul essence of defeated enemies to strengthen your soul power.
-- Convert absorbed soul energy into health, stamina, or spiritual reserves.
-- Temporarily gain the abilities or memories of absorbed souls.
[Because you have absorbed a very potent soul relic, the Guardian Protect sensing range has increased. You can now sense those under your protection within a 10-mile radius.]
[You have temporarily received the memories of Janice, the former guardian of the young Miss Li Hua, Daughter of the Shadows.]
[All other benefits will be unlocked as your soul grows.]
"Damn, what happened to just looking for a normal, small human?" Kent muttered, a small smile playing on his lips.

[Does the master want to seal the memories received from Janice?] the tower asked. The [Soul Absorb] ability allows him to temporarily gain access to the memories of those he has killed and whose souls he has absorbed.
This means that if he somehow learns the memories of others, he can only keep them temporarily; after that, they will vanish from his mind.

Even Janice’s blood was no longer there. Her body, too, was gone.

The next second, the body was burned, and Kent started moving further north. From the memories, Janice had managed to track them using her last breath to a location 40 miles away.
Kent wanted to believe that after traversing these 40 miles, he could find something.

Right now, Kent’s anger started to rise for obvious reasons. If before he just wanted to look for Li Hua, this time, he was determined to find those who dared kill her grandma and inflict on them the cruelest form of torture.

Now that he found out some people were after her and had killed her grandma, Kent was pissed.
Guardian or not, he wouldn’t forgive them.

chapters.title: Chapter 70: Daisy’s Scheme
paragraphs: Hours ago, after Kent left Li Hua’s cake shop following the directions given to him by the store lady. A young man in the store beside her closed his and left.
An hour later, he was kneeling in front of Dave and Daisy Ashland, who seemed to have just finished a round of sex. The two had been quite intimate recently.
In their minds, they had set the perfect trap for the Dark Cloth lady and were already anticipating reaping the benefits. So, even with nothing yet accomplished, they started to celebrate.
However, their celebration was cut short when the young man, one of their spies, brought them rather unusual news that could destroy their plans.
"Are you telling me those two without names are being sought out by a stranger?" Daisy asked with a slight frown.
"Yes, my lady," the young man replied, not daring to hesitate, fearing he might lose his life at any moment. He had heard that their Madam and Master had become something of a menace recently.
"Did you get a good look at this stranger?" Daisy asked.
"Yes. He is a young man, about 18 years old. He has long silver-purple hair and eyes matching the same hue. He is quite handsome and dressed well, probably a noble."
Daisy listened to her subordinate for a while. After he finished, she pondered on it for a few more seconds before a small smile formed on her lips.
She retrieved a small pouch from her space ring and threw it to the man. "Good job. Take that as a reward for bringing such good information."
The young man took the pouch and soon left the room. Once outside, he let out a good sigh and disappeared from the Ashland estate altogether.
Back inside the room, Daisy wore a smile on her face, which startled Dave. The Daisy he knew wouldn’t smile for no reason. That smile usually appeared only when her schemes were bearing fruit.
"What is it, my love?" Dave asked.
"Nothing much, just that we’ll be getting results sooner than we anticipated," Daisy replied, looking ecstatic.
"Really?" Dave’s expression relaxed noticeably.
"Yes. The stranger he talked about was the same alchemist who started this whole mess. If we capture him, we can blackmail his master into fighting and hopefully killing the Dark Cloth lady.

Of course, before anything else, we will have her sign a contract prohibiting her from revealing the truth afterward. Unless she wants to risk her soul being annihilated," Daisy explained, her tone brimming with confidence. Dave’s eyes widened in amazement.
"This is a brilliant plan, my love," Dave said, his mood visibly brightened.
"What do you need me to do?" he asked.

"Double—no, triple—the guards at the prison and make sure the perfect bait is placed to attract him. I know for a fact he’ll somehow find the prison. In fact, if possible, they should make it easy for him to find it.
Once he’s inside, they can ambush him, beat him up, and capture him. Once he’s in our custody, we can think of the next steps," Daisy instructed with a sly smile.

Dave smiled back. He trusted his woman and knew her well. Her plots always ended with them gaining more than they bargained for. For 50 years, she had devised many schemes, and at every turn, she came out on top.
This had made the Ashland Noble Family one of the kingdom’s most respected and powerful noble families.

Daisy was the brain, while Dave was the brawn. However, over the years, Dave had started to sense that his woman was far more ambitious than he had initially thought. She began contacting shady organizations, seeking help to rise above their current status.
Her dream was to become a queen, and she intended to use foreign powers to achieve that goal.
Everything had been going well until Kent appeared.

He had destroyed her first plot to steal Lilian’s spirit root for her daughter and then sell her to the shady organization. This move would have helped secure the family’s status as a legacy family, which means a step closer to the throne.
But Kent’s presence destroyed everything.
Still, her mind didn’t register the setback as a defeat. Instead, she saw a way forward and was now treading that path.
With the Sword Saintess Selene now in the picture, Daisy planned to use her to eliminate a troublesome variable. From there, she intended to move even further toward her ultimate goal.
If a spirit root was that useful to this shady organization, then how much would a rare body constitution cost?

Daisy had been researching Li Hua’s condition for a while. Somebody has told her about a rare body constitution that can fetch a fortune. Naturally, she had no reason to trust this person, but that doesn’t mean she didn’t look into Li Hua.
While many may see Li Hua as someone who might have an illness, which was why she was so small, Daisy knew better. However, she wasn’t sure. She wanted to wait and see how things progressed.
That was until the spirit root deal fell through. She quickly devised a new plan, and since she had the next best thing, she went for it.
Now, however, she was about to make a big move, and Kent would play a huge part in it. She couldn’t afford to lose again.
Unbeknownst to her, she had provoked a sleeping dragon when she moved her fangs toward Li Hua.
Coming after Lilian’s Spirit Root wasn’t something Kent cared about. He wasn’t going to pursue the matter. He left it for the Alderford family to handle.
He only wanted to have fun with the ladies. But the moment he set his sights on the small human, their destinies were interlinked.
They were somehow linked. But now that they had taken a step further and killed her guardian, they had accelerated things, and now, a dragon was marching toward them.
They had made the wrong move, and it was about to bite them where it hurt.
Naturally, this is what people call fate. But their fate is already sealed. Soon, the kingdom would know what Chaos feels like when a Guardian is provoked.
Dave Ashland left to carry out his woman’s order like an errand boy. A few minutes later, more guards were sent to the prison, where they planned to ambush Kent.
It was also the prison where Li Hua and someone else that fate seemed to be toying with were being held.
Hours later, Kent, who had just left the small shed in the woods, began making his way in the direction Janice had tracked the attackers.

He was in the forest, but all the beasts he sensed were weak, so they didn’t even notice him. Of course, a few tried to play hero, but those unfortunate ones died before they even realized what was happening.

It took Kent a couple of hours, but soon, he came upon a clearing where a battle seemed to have occurred. Judging by the beast carcasses scattered on the ground, it was clear the fight had been between humans and monsters.
Kent paused only briefly to track where they had gone. It took him just a moment to find their trail.
Thirty minutes later, the soul-tracking seal picked up on the target...

chapters.title: Chapter 71: Guardian’s Protect (1)
paragraphs: Immediately, the soul-tracking seal picked up on the target, and Kent halted in his steps. He wasn’t stopping because the person he sensed was a Level 5 Root Saint; he stopped because he wanted to prepare for what was to come.
He pulled up his status page.
[Status]+[Harem]+[Alchemy]+[Bloodline]+[Guardian]+[Soul Cultivator]
Name: Kent
Age: 18
Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon
Class: Alchemist
SubClass: Swordsman | Soul Cultivation
Cultivation: Root Master - Lvl 5/9
Physical Strength: 375
Physical Agility: 375
Physical Stamina: 455
Spiritual Strenght: 615
Mental Strength: 645
[You are much more powerful now, Master,] the tower commented, sounding proud. Kent could feel it.

"I have indeed become much stronger these past few days. However, a guardian can never be prepared enough, so I must be extra cautious. It’s just a gut feeling, but I can sense the danger moving toward me...
Or more like waiting for me," Kent sighed.
[How can I help, Master?] the tower asked.
Since it wasn’t a true system but more like a servant, Kent could ask for anything. According to its configuration, it would either accept the request if it benefited its master,
or reject it and offer a better option. Kent would then evaluate whether he liked the alternative or not. No decision would be made until they arrived at a solution that suited him.
"You can start by telling me how many I will be facing and the hidden dangers I might not be aware of," Kent asked. It was a long shot, but he had to try.
[I can help the master, but I will need to access the soul-tracking seal and use a part of the master’s soul strength,] the tower said.
Kent didn’t even think it over. "Go ahead."
He felt his soul strength being sucked out of his body for a few seconds before it was returned.
[I have used the connection to learn a few things. First, these people are known as Dark Legion guards. They are the elite guards of the Ashland Noble Family and among the best in the Kingdom.
They have 3,000 members, but currently, 170 are in the Dark Prison, where the young Miss Li Hua is being held.
Among the 170, 100 are in the Root Master stage, 60 are in the Root Grandmaster stage, and 10 are in the Root Saint Stage. However, among the ten, one is at the peak of the Root Saint stage.
Ironically, this one is also a swordsman with early-stage Grandmaster mastery. He has access to sword qi and sword intent, though his mastery over sword intent is still in the adept stage.
There is also a mage capable of casting powerful debuff spells.
The master might be out of his league here. But that is what makes it fun...]
Kent raised an eyebrow and was about to retort when a new set of messages appeared. Of course, he wasn’t surprised by the sudden messages.
[You have received a mega quest. This is your first time receiving this quest, so the rewards will be doubled.]
[Quest Name: Guardian’s Protect]
[Quest Description: A ward under your protection’s life is threatened. As a guardian, you are required to protect your ward with your life. Show your might.]
[Rewards: 4 Skill Upgrade Passes | The Rat’s Lair Medallion | A Hidden Reward]
"Looks like I have to bring my A-game here," Kent smiled. From the moment he appeared in this world, he had been longing for a good fight.
The last time he fought, it was one-sided because the targets were too weak. But not this time. The opponents were much more powerful.
"A level 5 Root Master against a Peak Saint, huh? I wish Master was here to witness this," Kent muttered.
[I can record it for the Master if you want.]
"Do that, buddy. Although she will believe me if I tell her, she would be very pleased to witness it, even if it’s just a video." Kent smiled.
If only he knew the decision to record the upcoming battle would become a key to knowing a lot about himself.
Before starting, he quickly assessed his points to see how he could improve his strength. A single him against 170 was already an overkill. The least he could do was level the playing field.
[Tower Points: 760,000]
[Attribute Points: 310]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 8100]
’Hmm, killing the spirit beast paid off some Skill Upgrade Points.’
"Tower, add 100 points to strength and agility, then 50 to stamina and spiritual strength, and the last 10 to mental strength."
[Points added.]
Kent felt a rush of energy pass through him, confirming the points had been distributed.
"I also have 8,100 points. How should I spend them, Tower?" Kent asked.

[Since the master already has some powerful sword techniques, the Elemental Manipulation skill can be weeded out for now. The Teleport skill is also strong enough, and even if it weren’t, there aren’t enough points to upgrade its grade or rank.
The 36 String Weaving Strike is also strong enough, but since we don’t have enough points for it, we can reserve that for later. After the battle, you can handle that.
Now, the only skill you have that doesn’t have much use just yet is the Appraiser’s Eye. For now, that skill is only a Rare-grade skill at the SS rank. It isn’t much, but it can be more.
But that would depend on whether the master wants to upgrade it or not. That said, the skill has great potential yet to be discovered.]
"The Appraiser’s Eye, huh? Why not. Tower, let’s upgrade that," Kent said.
[The master has two options, each of which will cost 5,000 points:
The first is to upgrade the skill’s grade from Rare to Earth grade, advancing the skill to the next level.
The second is to raise the rank from SS to SSS, strengthening and improving the already existing effects.]
"Go for the grade," Kent ordered.
[Command received. Upgrading skill... Appraiser’s Eye skill successfully upgraded from Rare Grade to Earth Grade.]
[You have upgraded your skill from Rare to Earth Grade. The Appraiser’s Eye skill has undergone great improvements. The skill has also undergone a name change.]
[Skill Name: Appraiser’s Eye (Max)]
[Grade: Earth]
[Rank: SS]
[Effects:]
-- With a simple glance, you can learn hidden details about people, beasts, items, and much more.
-- This skill has also enhanced your awareness. Your ability to read body language has reached a new height.
"This is good enough," Kent muttered.
He then extended calling for his weapon. Somewhere inside his room inside the Alderford Mansion, the sword sheath on his bed vanished and appeared in his hand.
[How is the Master going to approach this?] the Tower asked.
"I will be walking to their doorstep like I own the place," Kent said with a smile. Naturally, he was feeling pretty confident now.
[Good answer, Master,] the Tower responded, and then a new quest appeared.
[You have received a side quest.]
[Quest Name: Guardian’s Arrogance]
[Quest Description: Even though your ward is in trouble, walk with your shoulders high and show them what a Guardian is made of.]
[Reward: Kingdom Building Enchanted Book]
"Well then, here I come," Kent smiled and began walking toward the prison.

Spiritual Strenght: 615
Mental Strength: 645
[You are much more powerful now, Master,] the tower commented, sounding proud.
Kent could feel it.
"I have indeed become much stronger these past few days.
However, a guardian can never be prepared enough, so I must be extra cautious.
It’s just a gut feeling, but I can sense the danger moving toward me...
Or more like waiting for me," Kent sighed.
[How can I help, Master?] the tower asked.
Since it wasn’t a true system but more like a servant, Kent could ask for anything.
According to its configuration, it would either accept the request if it benefited its master,
or reject it and offer a better option.
Kent would then evaluate whether he liked the alternative or not.
No decision would be made until they arrived at a solution that suited him.
"You can start by telling me how many I will be facing and the hidden dangers I might not be aware of," Kent asked.
It was a long shot, but he had to try.
[I can help the master, but I will need to access the soul-tracking seal and use a part of the master’s soul strength,] the tower said.
Kent didn’t even think it over.
"Go ahead."
He felt his soul strength being sucked out of his body for a few seconds before it was returned.
[I have used the connection to learn a few things.
First, these people are known as Dark Legion guards.
They are the elite guards of the Ashland Noble Family and among the best in the Kingdom.
They have 3,000 members, but currently, 170 are in the Dark Prison, where the young Miss Li Hua is being held.
Among the 170, 100 are in the Root Master stage, 60 are in the Root Grandmaster stage, and 10 are in the Root Saint Stage.
However, among the ten, one is at the peak of the Root Saint stage.
Ironically, this one is also a swordsman with early-stage Grandmaster mastery.
He has access to sword qi and sword intent, though his mastery over sword intent is still in the adept stage.
There is also a mage capable of casting powerful debuff spells.
The master might be out of his league here.
But that is what makes it fun...]
Kent raised an eyebrow and was about to retort when a new set of messages appeared.
Of course, he wasn’t surprised by the sudden messages.
[You have received a mega quest.
This is your first time receiving this quest, so the rewards will be doubled.]
[Quest Name: Guardian’s Protect]
[Quest Description: A ward under your protection’s life is threatened.
As a guardian, you are required to protect your ward with your life.
Show your might.]
[Rewards: 4 Skill Upgrade Passes | The Rat’s Lair Medallion | A Hidden Reward]
"Looks like I have to bring my A-game here," Kent smiled.
From the moment he appeared in this world, he had been longing for a good fight.
The last time he fought, it was one-sided because the targets were too weak.
But not this time.
The opponents were much more powerful.
"A level 5 Root Master against a Peak Saint, huh?
I wish Master was here to witness this," Kent muttered.
[I can record it for the Master if you want.]
"Do that, buddy.
Although she will believe me if I tell her, she would be very pleased to witness it, even if it’s just a video." Kent smiled.
If only he knew the decision to record the upcoming battle would become a key to knowing a lot about himself.
Before starting, he quickly assessed his points to see how he could improve his strength.
A single him against 170 was already an overkill.
The least he could do was level the playing field.
[Tower Points: 760,000]
[Attribute Points: 310]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 8100]
’Hmm, killing the spirit beast paid off some Skill Upgrade Points.’
"Tower, add 100 points to strength and agility, then 50 to stamina and spiritual strength, and the last 10 to mental strength."
[Points added.]
Kent felt a rush of energy pass through him, confirming the points had been distributed.
"I also have 8,100 points.
How should I spend them, Tower?" Kent asked.
[Since the master already has some powerful sword techniques, the Elemental Manipulation skill can be weeded out for now.
The Teleport skill is also strong enough, and even if it weren’t, there aren’t enough points to upgrade its grade or rank.
The 36 String Weaving Strike is also strong enough, but since we don’t have enough points for it, we can reserve that for later.
After the battle, you can handle that.
Now, the only skill you have that doesn’t have much use just yet is the Appraiser’s Eye.
For now, that skill is only a Rare-grade skill at the SS rank.
It isn’t much, but it can be more.
But that would depend on whether the master wants to upgrade it or not.
That said, the skill has great potential yet to be discovered.]
"The Appraiser’s Eye, huh?
Why not.
Tower, let’s upgrade that," Kent said.
[The master has two options, each of which will cost 5,000 points:
The first is to upgrade the skill’s grade from Rare to Earth grade, advancing the skill to the next level.
The second is to raise the rank from SS to SSS, strengthening and improving the already existing effects.]
"Go for the grade," Kent ordered.
[Command received.
Upgrading skill...
Appraiser’s Eye skill successfully upgraded from Rare Grade to Earth Grade.]
[You have upgraded your skill from Rare to Earth Grade.
The Appraiser’s Eye skill has undergone great improvements.
The skill has also undergone a name change.]
[Skill Name: Appraiser’s Eye (Max)]
[Grade: Earth]
[Rank: SS]
[Effects:]
-- With a simple glance, you can learn hidden details about people, beasts, items, and much more.
-- This skill has also enhanced your awareness.
Your ability to read body language has reached a new height.
"This is good enough," Kent muttered.
He then extended calling for his weapon.
Somewhere inside his room inside the Alderford Mansion, the sword sheath on his bed vanished and appeared in his hand.
[How is the Master going to approach this?] the Tower asked.
"I will be walking to their doorstep like I own the place," Kent said with a smile.
Naturally, he was feeling pretty confident now.
[Good answer, Master,] the Tower responded, and then a new quest appeared.
[You have received a side quest.]
[Quest Name: Guardian’s Arrogance]
[Quest Description: Even though your ward is in trouble, walk with your shoulders high and show them what a Guardian is made of.]
[Reward: Kingdom Building Enchanted Book]
"Well then, here I come," Kent smiled and began walking toward the prison.

chapters.title: Chapter 72: Guardian’s Protect (2)
paragraphs: "I can’t believe the leader thought 70 of us can’t handle a single Root Master, so he sent a hundred more," a young man said, showing an annoyed expression.

"Falk, you have to trust in the leader and what he does. If I am not mistaken, this was a direct instruction from Lady Daisy. We have to obey without question," another man said to the one named Falk.
"I know, leader. It’s just that seeing 170 of us guarding a mortal from a mere Root Master, I can’t help but feel like I was being looked down on," Falk stated.
He was one of the three people who went to kidnap Li Hua and also the same person who killed Li Hua’s grandmother, Janice.
As a Level 5 Root Saint, he felt like getting reinforcements to guard a mortal from Kent was an insult to his pride as a warrior. Of course, their leader, who goes by the name Vogt, felt the same.

The two were tribesmen who, after a pack of Bloodthirsty Hellhounds raided their tribe, chose to become retainers of the Ashland Noble family. Luckily, they landed roles in the Dark Legion guards and have been rising through the ranks ever since.
"That said, we should prepare to greet our guests warmly. Tell the others to prepare the torture room. We will have some time with him to lighten our mood," Vogt said, smiling slightly.
Falk nodded and left with a small smile. Clearly, they didn’t place Kent in their eyes. Naturally, it was natural, considering Kent was also moving toward them with calm and casual steps.
Just as they didn’t regard him, he didn’t regard them either. Right now, Kent was focused on one thing: rescuing the lamb under his care that had been taken away.

After all, as the wise saying goes, "What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?"
Kent was coming to rescue his lamb, and there was no way he would leave without it.
Thirty minutes after Kent finished preparing, a small mountain that seemed to be made into a cave prison appeared in his sight.
Immediately, he used his new and improved Appraiser’s Eye to appraise the mountain.
[Mokasa Mountain Prison]
[Danger: High]
-- This is a prison where the Dark Legion Guards, infamous for their ruthlessness and brutality, practice their immoral arts.
-- Anyone sent to this place never returns home, as the prison is designed for killing and erasing people from existence.
-- To date, 20,000 people have been executed in this prison, their deaths brought about through relentless torture until their hearts finally give out.
"Damn, these people are animals," Kent muttered, his expression calm.
Soon, he came within a 10-mile radius. The moment he entered the region, he sensed Li Hua through the guardian link between them.
"Tower, what is her condition?" Kent asked.
[She is well. No harm has come to her.]
To confirm, Kent moved forward, and his divine sense picked up on her. She was asleep in a small cell that seemed to haven’t been cleaned in forever.

Naturally, the moment his senses locked onto Li Hua, his presence was made known. But Kent didn’t panic. Instead, as soon as he felt himself being detected, he used his teleportation skill to close the gap.
The next second, he was only a few meters away.
However, he wouldn’t get a chance to enter the prison, as the entire area was immediately surrounded. Despite this, Kent kept moving until he was 100 meters from the prison entrance.
He looked around as if surveying a field of dead goats. After taking in the disdainful faces staring back at him, Kent sighed and rested his gaze on a man whose sharp eyes stood out among the crowd.
Instantly, Kent recognized the aura surrounding him and knew he was the leader.
"A swordsman," he muttered before accessing the man’s information.
[Name: Vogt Adler]
[Cultivation: Peak Root Saint]
[Danger: Very High]
-- Vogt is the leader of the Dark Legion Guards in the Makosa Mountain prison.
-- He is a swordsman who has mastered both sword qi and sword intent.

-- He was once a member of the Weiss Tribe, located somewhere in the Adira Mountains. After his tribe was raided and its members scattered, he joined the Dark Legion Guards with his brother and quickly rose through the ranks.
-- Throughout his career as a guard, he has killed 4,702 people, both innocent and guilty.
-- Known as the Blood Sword, Vogt earned his title because, after every battle, his sword is dyed red. He is extremely dangerous.
Skills:
- Blood Cut (Earth, SS)
- Solar Slash (Earth, S)
- Ashland Sword Art (Heaven, SS)
Kent didn’t say anything. Instead, he turned his attention to the next person who smelt of danger and scanned him, too. Naturally, they didn’t know what he was doing.
[Falk Adler]
[Cultivation: Level 5 Root Saint]
[Danger: High]
-- Falk is the vice leader of the Dark Legion Guards in the Makosa Mountain Prison.
-- He is a spearman who has mastered spear qi and quick precision attacks.
-- Known for his cruelty, Falk enjoys torturing prisoners for days before killing them.
-- He gained his position by eliminating anyone who challenged him, including his own comrades.
-- Falk is feared for his "Death Spiral" technique, which leaves his victims in pieces.
-- Many whisper that Falk’s spear is cursed, as it drips with blood that never dries.
Skills:
- Death Spiral (Earth, S)
- Shadow Lunge (Earth, A)
- Crimson Spear Art (Heaven, S)
Kent then looked for the mage that could pose a threat to him. The Tower did mention there is a mage that has some nasty debuff skills. Kent looked for him next.
It took just a few seconds to locate him. He was near the leader despite his cultivation base.
[Henry Ky Tay]
[Cultivation: Level 9 Root Master]
[Danger: Very High]
-- Henry is a mage who specializes in debuff spells.
-- His magic weakens his enemies, making them slow and vulnerable.
-- Known for his sadistic nature, Henry enjoys watching others suffer as their strength is drained away.
-- He can cripple entire groups of enemies by casting debilitating spells that affect their minds and bodies.
-- His dark magic can cause hallucinations, making his victims believe they are being attacked by their own allies.
Skills:
- Soul Drain (Heaven, SS)
- Mind Distort (Earth, SS)
- Venomous Curse (Earth, S)
’Bunch of nasty humans, I am going to enjoy killing them,’ Kent thought, then he looked back at Vogt, who stood with a nonchalant look on his face.
"Before I say what I have come here to do, he must first die," Kent said, turning his attention back to Henry.
The next second, a disc-shaped artifact appeared in his hand, and then he threw it.
The disc zipped fast through the air, and before they could react, a head came rolling down. The disc then flew back to Kent, who immediately threw it into his space ring.
Kent has finally used the [Instant Killing Disc]. Since Henry was a Root Master, he could easily kill him using the disc.
The next second, Vogt’s anger appeared when he saw his most valuable asset’s head on the floor. His sword appeared in his grip.
But before he could move, Kent raised his finger, signaling him to stop.
"Gentlemen, my name is Kent. I am a guardian, and you have someone who belongs to me. Naturally, I am here to retrieve her. But first, you all have to die" Kent spoke, his voice cold.
[Now, that is what you call an entrance...Kekekeke] The tower commented.

chapters.title: Chapter 73: Guardian’s Protect (3)
paragraphs: The guards’ faces turned ashen. Watching the head of their most valuable member on the ground was a huge blow to them.
They wouldn’t accept that. But before they moved, they first had to gain the permission of their leader, who at the moment was frozen in his tracks, watching Kent with bloodshot eyes.
Kent, too, was watching him with eyes full of disdain. He never expected to use the Instant Killing Disc he had earned from the quest when he added Unity to his harem.
But needing a quick method to kill the most dangerous person who could endanger his life, Kent had to use it. At most, he would need three days to charge it back before he could use it again.
"Like I said, I am a guardian, and you losers have taken someone who belongs to me. Naturally, I want her back.
But you guys are not the kind who would heed my request, so I will have to kill you all and take her away. Don’t even think about running because you can’t."
Immediately Kent said those words, his sword came out of the sheath, and his sword qi and intent surged.
The guards whose faces were full of disdain, immediately turned pale as they felt the pressure surrounding them.
"ATTACK!"
Of course, Vogt gave the order, sending his men to their deaths.
Kent smiled, but then the smile vanished, and his mood shifted.
He moved, and in place of where he was, 36 strings were woven from sword qi appeared. Three guards were unfortunate enough to be in the path of that attack.
The 36 strings passed through them, leaving only chunks of their body parts behind.
Vogt’s eyes narrowed when he saw how three of his finest were killed. He immediately knew why they were given reinforcement.
Of course, in reality, the reinforcement wasn’t because they overestimated Kent. No, they got the reinforcement to make sure he was caught and beaten in ways he couldn’t have imagined.
They only saw him as a mere Root Master, but in truth, they underestimated him.
"Surround him. Don’t give him an opening to attack," Vogt ordered, watching Kent appear 20 meters away from where he had killed the three guards.
He didn’t know how he moved, but he was keen on tracking him. Of course, he picked up on the teleport skill the next second, but it wasn’t as he expected.

Kent teleported all right, but when he appeared, he just blinked out of existence and then appeared in a different place. The place he was and where he appeared were random, and the distance was also not the same.
’What is this?’ Vogt suddenly had a bad feeling in the back of his mind.

Then Kent chose to make him feel it. The next second, Kent executed a series of rapid slashes before he vanished away. However, while he was away, the first form of the Annihilation Sword Technique was unleashed.
Dozens of sword arcs flashed through the air, catching seven people off guard. They were sliced into chunks of meat. Kent’s attacks were happening randomly and quickly, so they couldn’t track him.

Of course, the [Rapid Slash], which is the first form of the Annihilation Sword technique he received from Vexthra through Unity, was more powerful than he was using it. But Kent wasn’t overdoing it either.
The reason is simple: he doesn’t have the cultivation base to unleash even the first form in its full capacity. But that doesn’t mean he could only unleash a dozen Rapid Slashes either.
The reason he wasn’t using the skill with his full cultivation base was that he was doing something else aside from killing the guards.
Now that he has become a Soul Cultivator, he has more avenues to grow. It was why he was using the [Soul Absorb] skill to absorb the soul essence of those he was killing.
The skill allows him to absorb the soul essence of those he had killed with his hands.
He was killing multiple birds with one stone.
Skill upgrade points, Tower points, and Soul Essence were pouring in as he moved. For now, he was only using the [Annihilation Sword] with the first form, the [Rapid Slash] to run the field.
Kent wasn’t rushing it like he had anticipated. First, all the 170 guards were outside, meaning Li Hua was safe, and second, the person who could have given him a hard time was dead.
With Henry dead, there wouldn’t be any nasty debuff spells raining down on him. He wouldn’t be weakened to the point where he would have been unable to move his limbs.
Taking Henry out had removed that scenario. So for now, he was having a field day with the others. Of course, he was also cautious of two more people.
Vogt and Falk hadn’t attacked yet, but he wasn’t worried much, considering none of them could lock down on him with how fast he was moving.
But even if they did, he could break it. He hadn’t unleashed his aura yet, and it was for a very important moment that hadn’t arrived yet.
One could say Kent had overestimated his targets, and now, he was getting bored.
"Nine Calamities sword strike: True Despair sword strike."
Suddenly, Kent roared and unleashed the first form of the technique he received from his sword sheath. A powerful sword light flashed forward at the guards.
The guards who were on the receiving end of the sword strike immediately felt despair. Their faces paled, and their legs turned to jelly.
They could only wait for the sword light, made of sword qi and strengthened by the intent of Hatred and Resentment, to devour them.
Kent smiled.
"Elemental Manipulation: Fire Lion Strike."
Kent unleashed yet another attack, but this time, instead of sword qi, a flaming lion was slashed out of the sword and bathed four guards in a blue inferno.
Kent smiled again. This time, he used the elemental manipulation skill to unleash a sword attack. The skill allowed him to channel his element through his sword.
He didn’t know much about flame manipulation for combat, but with his knowledge of alchemy, he had mastered one move: the Fire Lion Strike.
He had seen this lion on his way to the prison, and right now, he was testing whether it would work as he anticipated.
Of course, with four people set aflame, the technique seemed to be a success. The only thing left was for him to master how to fuse the sword qi into it.
But since it worked, he didn’t stop.
Soon, fire lion after fire lion filled the place. Kent wasn’t holding back.
Soon, 70% were dead, but Vogt and Falk still hadn’t attacked. They kept issuing orders, but none made a move. Perhaps they wanted to wait until he was done killing every last one of their guards.
And Kent was doing it. He was killing them. 90% were dead, leaving only a handful. But the two strongest still haven’t made a move.
The other Saints came forward, but Kent was killing them without mercy. Of course, he wasn’t taking his eyes off the two.

[Master, the ones named Vogt and Falk are about to use a technique to escape, but they wouldn’t leave alone. They seem to have placed a seal on the young miss. The technique will activate in 5 seconds, and it requires two people.]
’What?’
Kent teleported instantly. The next second, his sword was embedded in Falk’s chest. The technique was canceled, and Vogt received a backlash. But then he attacked.
"Ashland Sword Art: First form, Blinding Slash!"
