The reason is simple: he doesn’t have the cultivation base to unleash even the first form in its full capacity.
But that doesn’t mean he could only unleash a dozen Rapid Slashes either.
The reason he wasn’t using the skill with his full cultivation base was that he was doing something else aside from killing the guards.
Now that he has become a Soul Cultivator, he has more avenues to grow.
It was why he was using the [Soul Absorb] skill to absorb the soul essence of those he was killing.
The skill allows him to absorb the soul essence of those he had killed with his hands.
He was killing multiple birds with one stone.
Skill upgrade points, Tower points, and Soul Essence were pouring in as he moved.
For now, he was only using the [Annihilation Sword] with the first form, the [Rapid Slash] to run the field.
Kent wasn’t rushing it like he had anticipated.
First, all the 170 guards were outside, meaning Li Hua was safe, and second, the person who could have given him a hard time was dead.
With Henry dead, there wouldn’t be any nasty debuff spells raining down on him.
He wouldn’t be weakened to the point where he would have been unable to move his limbs.
Taking Henry out had removed that scenario.
So for now, he was having a field day with the others.
Of course, he was also cautious of two more people.
Vogt and Falk hadn’t attacked yet, but he wasn’t worried much, considering none of them could lock down on him with how fast he was moving.
But even if they did, he could break it.
He hadn’t unleashed his aura yet, and it was for a very important moment that hadn’t arrived yet.
One could say Kent had overestimated his targets, and now, he was getting bored.
"Nine Calamities sword strike: True Despair sword strike."
Suddenly, Kent roared and unleashed the first form of the technique he received from his sword sheath.
A powerful sword light flashed forward at the guards.
The guards who were on the receiving end of the sword strike immediately felt despair.
Their faces paled, and their legs turned to jelly.
They could only wait for the sword light, made of sword qi and strengthened by the intent of Hatred and Resentment, to devour them.
Kent smiled.
"Elemental Manipulation: Fire Lion Strike."
Kent unleashed yet another attack, but this time, instead of sword qi, a flaming lion was slashed out of the sword and bathed four guards in a blue inferno.
Kent smiled again.
This time, he used the elemental manipulation skill to unleash a sword attack.
The skill allowed him to channel his element through his sword.
He didn’t know much about flame manipulation for combat, but with his knowledge of alchemy, he had mastered one move: the Fire Lion Strike.
He had seen this lion on his way to the prison, and right now, he was testing whether it would work as he anticipated.
Of course, with four people set aflame, the technique seemed to be a success.
The only thing left was for him to master how to fuse the sword qi into it.
But since it worked, he didn’t stop.
Soon, fire lion after fire lion filled the place.
Kent wasn’t holding back.
Soon, 70% were dead, but Vogt and Falk still hadn’t attacked.
They kept issuing orders, but none made a move.
Perhaps they wanted to wait until he was done killing every last one of their guards.
And Kent was doing it.
He was killing them.
90% were dead, leaving only a handful.
But the two strongest still haven’t made a move.
The other Saints came forward, but Kent was killing them without mercy.
Of course, he wasn’t taking his eyes off the two.
[Master, the ones named Vogt and Falk are about to use a technique to escape, but they wouldn’t leave alone.
They seem to have placed a seal on the young miss.
The technique will activate in 5 seconds, and it requires two people.]
’What?’
Kent teleported instantly.
The next second, his sword was embedded in Falk’s chest.
The technique was canceled, and Vogt received a backlash.
But then he attacked.
"Ashland Sword Art: First form, Blinding Slash!"

chapters.title: Chapter 74: Unexpected but Expected Trap
paragraphs: Falk’s head was on the floor, and 12 other Dark Legion Guards were about to escape. Vogt unleashed an attack at Kent, who just smiled and teleported away.

Everything was happening so fast that Vogt didn’t know how it all ended in such a state. Vogt and Falk were opportunists. Their loyalty was to the highest bidder, so they never truly had the Ashland family at heart.
This was also why Falk was mad when they received reinforcements a few days ago. They didn’t want more soldiers because they never planned to hand over Li Hua to the Ashland family.
Their plan was very simple: when Kent appeared, they would kill him and their men and then run off with Li Hua, intending to sell her to the highest bidder.
They knew she was special, considering the Ashland Noble Family had gone through a lot for her. Naturally, they wouldn’t let such a chance to cash out pass.
Their plan was airtight. They had secured a Tier 3 teleportation talisman that required 5 minutes to activate.
They planned to use it to leave the place since the talisman was designed to wipe their existence from the location once it was used. It could not be tracked.
They had also bought body doubles from an artisan and planned to fake their deaths after killing their men. So, getting more reinforcements was a headache.
However, when Kent appeared and started killing with ease, they decided to put their plan into motion, and they nearly succeeded.
However, they failed to notice one thing: the man they were facing had an overprotective tower that was always looking for ways to keep its master safe.
Although not an actual system, the tower could do much more now that Kent’s soul strength was relatively high.

Now that Kent had become a Soul Master, the tower had grown much stronger and more active. It had already started finding ways to help its master grow even more powerful, and, well, the method it envisioned was a slaughter.
Kent teleported away, causing Vogt’s sword attack to slice through empty air. He reappeared the next moment, and a head rolled to the floor.
[You have slain a Level 2 Root Saint, Kojo Cue]
[Your soul grows stronger.]
[Current Soul essence: 1004/2004]
Kent was absorbing the soul essence of the guards he was killing. Though he hadn’t leveled up his Soul Cultivation subclass yet, he could feel his soul growing stronger by the second.
He moved to his next target, then teleported back to Vogt, who was still recovering from his missed attack.
Kent spared him no pity and unleashed the [36 String Weaving Strike], demanding Vogt’s full attention and forcing him to defend.

Kent vanished, leaving the attack behind for Vogt to handle. Vogt’s sword qi surged, and his intent fully awakened as he unleashed a series of [Blood Cuts], sending deep red sword arcs slicing through the air at the blinding speed of the 36-string strike.
By the time Vogt finished defending, Kent had already killed two more guards, bringing their number down to eight.
Kent unleashed two [Fire Lion Strikes] before repeating the same tactic. After two more rounds, only two guards remained. This time, Kent didn’t bother repeating his strategy.
He moved swiftly, removing their heads from their bodies. When he was done, he turned to face Vogt, who now wore a tired and pale expression.
While he looked tired, his aura and cultivation base still seemed sharp. However, it wasn’t affecting Kent at all. It felt nonexistent.
The reason was simple: Kent’s stats had been boosted by 500%.
When he acquired the skill [Guardian’s Protect] skill, he had expected it to activate only when a ward under his protection was in danger. Of course, this was a miscalculation on his part.

The skill activated when he came within two miles of Li Hua. Although she hadn’t been harmed in any way, she had been knocked out with a drug. But even without that, just kidnapping her was a grave mistake on their part.
Additionally, Kent had grown stronger after distributing his points and absorbing 169 soul essences. Even without using his aura, the peak Saint in front of him posed no threat.
His anger was evident, but he maintained a clear mind.
"Who are you?" Vogt asked, his grip on his sword tightening. He could feel it—his aura wasn’t affecting Kent. That troubled him greatly.
"Just a humble Guardian looking for his ward," Kent muttered coldly.
"Why are you doing this? Who would go this far for a mere mortal?" Vogt demanded.
The heads of his men lay on the floor. While he didn’t care about them, the only person he cared about was now headless on the ground.
"Like I said, I am here for my ward." Kent moved forward and thrust his sword at Vogt’s heart. But at the last moment, Kent abandoned the attack and turned while slashing his sword behind him.
Clang!
A spinning disc collided with Kent’s sword, sending him flying backward. He slammed into the ground and coughed up two mouthfuls of blood.
Unfortunately, Vogt, whom Kent planned to kill and absorb memories from, was in the path of the disc that deflected off Kent’s sword.
The disc sliced through him, splitting him in half. Kent’s plan to learn more about the Ashland Family was ruined.
But he didn’t have the luxury to dwell on that. The Tower had warned him about this possibly being a major trap.
It was indeed a trap.
Hovering ahead was a woman with a frowning mask covering her face. She was clad in dark armor, and judging by the aura around her, she was a Peak Root Sage.
Naturally, she was releasing her aura to intimidate Kent who had killed 170 people in less than ten minutes.
She wasn’t underestimating him.
[Master, I have locked onto the young miss. Just give the word, and we are out of here. Although your soul is not strong enough to handle teleportation easily, you won’t die either.]
<Hold on for now, Tower,> Kent replied as he gazed at the masked woman and asked,
"Who are you?"

He already had a plan in mind. The Tower would use his soul energy to teleport both him and Li Hua away. However, the backlash could render him unconscious for up to half a year. Kent didn’t want that outcome.
Not while he still had some way out.

"The question should be, who are you, young man? I’ve encountered many humans with great potential, but none quite like you," the masked woman said coldly. She moved closer, stopping just a meter away from Kent.
Kent instinctively took a few steps back.
"Tell me, young man, what is your name?" the woman asked.
"I asked the question first," Kent replied, his gaze steady on the woman. He knew he couldn’t defeat her but refused to cower before her.
"A bold one, huh? I like that," she said. "Initially, I planned to kill you since I can’t leave any witnesses when I claim the Atomic Divine Body. But I’ve changed my mind.
"With your potential, having you as my slave would be far more advantageous. So, human, will you become my slave willingly, or do you prefer the hard way?"
The moment Kent heard her question, something shifted within him. "What did you just say?" he asked, his voice chilling as the temperature around them dropped.
Then, everything went dark. Kent blacked out.

chapters.title: Chapter 75: Unexpected Outcome
paragraphs: A few days ago, after the dark-clothed lady left the Ashland Mansions, she didn’t immediately leave the vicinity.
She was just a few meters away from the mansion when Daisy and Dave Ashland concocted their plan to have her killed using Kent’s master.
Of course, she didn’t like the idea; however, she remained calm and manipulated them as they intended to manipulate him.
For days, she stayed there, monitoring their movements. When she heard of an Atomic Divine Body, her greed surfaced, and she decided to claim it for herself and her secret organization.
She knew that once she enslaved Li Hua and introduced her to the Dark Devil Church, her ranking would rise, and she might gain more authority to extend her reach.
The idea excited her. So she waited until hours ago when she overheard Daisy and Dave talking about someone tracking the Atomic Divine Body and that they would be sending reinforcements.
Naturally, it was the moment she had been waiting for, considering she had never known the location of where the Atomic Body was held.
But with the soldiers now deployed there, she followed them and then waited. She expected many things to happen.
The first was a powerful person coming with Kent, considering she had learned he was the disciple of the woman who had dealt her the greatest defeat.
Fifteen years ago, she had nearly died when she chose the saintess as her first kill to fully initiate herself into the Dark Devil Church.
This failure set her back many years and ranks. So, she was waiting for Kent to go and ask for reinforcement from his master.
She wanted that, mainly because she sought to kill the saintess and avenge her humiliation years ago. This time, she had prepared well and intended to use the element of surprise to kill her.
But then Kent appeared, and she had to make changes to her plan.
She wanted the guards to kill the overly confident Kent, after which she would use his dead body to taunt the saintess.
But that plan also failed.

So, she formed a new one. Since Kent had proven to be a very powerful human with untapped potential, she decided to steal him from the saintess and make him her slave. Naturally, she would have succeeded.
But her mistake was not killing Kent rather than her dream of making him her slave.
Her mistake was threatening a Primordial Chaos Dragon with slavery.
That was why, at that very moment, she had a sword through her heart, blood dripping from her mouth and nostrils, and a look that screamed one thing: fear in her eyes.
She was terrified beyond measure. Blood drenched her entire body, and the very air around her was as sharp as a million tiny swords. The scene was surreal, but what was even more bizarre was Kent.
His appearance.
His demeanor.
His presence.

The Kent standing before the dark lady, Lady Sandra—widely known in the Dark Devil Church—was a completely different person. He looked like Kent, but he didn’t feel like Kent. The Kent before her now was like a devil who thrived on slaughter.
The aura around him is full of hate and resentment.
Lady Sandra was shivering as her life force and soul essence were draining rapidly through a runic rope that had pierced her forehead.
Five minutes later, Lady Sandra fell back and died. Then the runic rope coiled. Without casting a look at her, Kent formed a series of hand seals and muttered something.
The runic rope coiled tighter, and a red bead about the size of an adult’s thumb appeared after a few seconds. The energy radiating from it was pure soul energy.
Then Kent fell back and collapsed.

Immediately, Kent collapsed, and his body began exuding a potent, chaotic energy. His skin started changing as dark red dragon scales appeared. Within moments, his entire body was covered in tiny, intricate dragon scales.
The chaotic energy radiating from him gradually calmed down. Ten hours later, around 7 in the morning, Kent woke up amidst a gruesome scene of headless bodies.
"My head..." he muttered, clutching his temples.
His vision was blurry, and the sight around him was far from pleasant. Fortunately, he could close his eyes and communicate with the tower.
<What happened, Tower?> Kent asked.
[You blacked out, Master,] the tower responded.
Indeed, Kent had blacked out right after Lady Sandra threatened to turn him into her slave.
But that wasn’t all that happened. He knew something significant had occurred. The fact that he was still alive and free of any slave seal confirmed that he hadn’t been captured.
To confirm further, he carefully opened his eyes. There, lying before him, was the lifeless body of the woman who had threatened him.
Yet the question lingered: how had he been able to kill a peak Root Sage when he knew he wouldn’t have survived a single attack from her?
<Tower, what happened after I blacked out?> he asked again.
If anyone could answer his questions, it was the tower.
[You killed the lady after you blacked out, Master,] the tower replied.
Kent wasn’t convinced. The idea that he had killed the woman with his own hands felt improbable.
"Did I really kill her? But why can’t I remember anything about the fight—how it started and how it ended?"
Kent was utterly confused. None of it made sense. Yet, he knew one thing: blacking out often meant losing all recollection of what happened next.
But then he also knew that sometimes, you could indeed remember what happened after you blacked out. That is if you were recording it.
<Tower, do you have a recording of the battle? You said you would record it,> Kent asked, fingers crossed.
[Video has been recorded and is now rendering. Estimated time until full rendering: 7 days.]

[Because the master’s soul isn’t that strong, depending too much on the tower would affect your health. So, I am using only a sliver of your soul to run this process. Using more soul energy will have a negative effect.]
"I see. At least everything will be made known in 7 days," Kent sighed.
He stood up and went to retrieve his sword. However, the moment he stood up, he saw a red bead radiating intense soul energy a few steps behind him.
Kent quickly moved and picked it up. His Appraiser’s Eye then scanned it.
[Extreme Soul Bead (Forbidden Pill)]
[Grade: Tier 7]
-- This bead has been condensed from a human’s soul and life force. It has also been amplified using forbidden dark magic, making it 3000 times more potent.
-- But although the bead is forbidden, it contains the purest form of soul energy.
-- Absorbing this bead will enhance one’s soul in many ways. It also nurtures the soul and makes it very rich in concentration.
-- It is said that if a soul cultivator absorbs a soul bead, their chances of forming a soul body are very high. It also improves the spirit root to a certain degree.
"Looks like good stuff," Kent muttered as he quickly placed the bead in his space ring and went to retrieve his sword.
He gazed at the scared expression on Lady Sandra’s face and smirked.
"Serves you right. Wanting to make me your slave... How bold!" Subconsciously, Kent leaked a very powerful aura that shouldn’t belong to a Level 5 Root Master.
He entered the cave where Li Hua had just woken up and held a lost expression on her cute little face.

He entered the cave where Li Hua had just woken up and held a lost expression on her cute little face.

chapters.title: Chapter 76: Rescued & Promised
paragraphs: Kent quickly entered the cave, which is considered one of the most notorious spaces in the kingdom. Few knew of its existence, and even fewer spoke of it, for no one was supposed to.
The atrocities that occurred there were too barbaric to recount.
Those sent there never returned. It was a place meant for one purpose: to die screaming. Vogt and Falk were anything but benevolent.
When Kent stepped inside, he saw smaller cells with chains hanging from the walls.
[Master, those chains are enchanted to strip one of their cultivation base when put on. They also inflict mental torture and soul deprivation.]
<How sinister. Thankfully, I beheaded them all.> Kent sighed and kept moving.
A few seconds later, he stopped in front of a cell. Inside, a small human girl sat, her gaze unfocused and dazed.
The moment her eyes landed on Kent, she froze. She tried to stand but couldn’t; the potion’s effects still left her weak and drowsy.
"Big brother..." she called out in a frail voice, her mouth and eyes wide open.
For some reason, Kent’s anger resurfaced when he saw her in that state. His sword came out of the sheath and returned the next moment, but the door was cut open, and he quickly stepped in.
"Big Brother", Li Hua’s tears started to flow.
"Big brother... they killed Grandma, they killed Grandma," her tears were overflowing now that she had seen a familiar face.

Although she had only known Kent for two minutes, she could tell he wasn’t there to hurt her. Just as Kent was angry when he saw her weak self, she also felt vulnerable and an instant trust when she saw him.

This was because of the connection between them. The guardianship would always make Kent aware of her and even know when she was in trouble. Of course, that was how it would be if he had fully awakened the Guardian Tower.
"Calm down, Li Hua. You are safe now," Kent said, rubbing her small head as he let the tiny human cry her heart out.
Everyone was dead now. He wasn’t in a hurry to leave. In fact, Kent was hoping more guards would come so he could vent his anger.
An hour later, Li Hua calmed down. Initially, Kent was worried about how to approach the matter of her Grandma’s/Guardian’s death, but hearing and seeing that she already knew calmed him down a bit.
The memory he had locked away could have helped him, but he wasn’t thinking about that just yet.
For now, Kent was very angry, and this was due to his [Guardian Protect] skill. Because of this, Kent would seek revenge on those who dared to hurt someone under his protection.
"Take this," Kent said, grabbing a pill from his space ring and placing it on Li Hua’s tongue. The pill dissolved in her mouth, filling her with energy.
"Big Brother, are you here to rescue me?" Li Hua asked, a little more composed now.
"Yes. Your Grandma told me to come when I came looking for you," Kent said with a small smile, trying to ease her anxious heart.
"Grandma," Li Hua muttered, wiping an invisible tear from her eyes. "I miss Grandma," she said.
She had been present when her Grandma was killed and had witnessed it all.
Perhaps the kidnappers wanted her to know there was no coming back for her. By killing her only attachment, they were telling her she had no hope of being freed.
Of course, for some reason, that part of the memory was buried deep in the memory Kent received from Janice.
He didn’t know why, but he could tell the Fox Lady didn’t want him to know. He would later sit down and go through her memories and the new ones he had extracted despite blacking out.
"Don’t worry, Li Hua, big brother is going to protect you now. I will ensure no harm comes to you, no matter the danger," Kent promised.
"Mmm," Li Hua nodded her tiny head, holding Kent’s hand firmly.
A promise from a guardian is said to be the most dangerous vow. The epic saga of the untamed guardian—the one who rose through the heavens, hunting all that threatened his ward.
The one who moved across realms to exact revenge on those who dared hurt his ward. The one who broke the heavens and killed gods just because they set their sights on his ward.
The heavens are about to understand the true nature of a guardian. One who fights relentlessly for his wards. One who is wholly dedicated to those he dares to place under his care.
Many will grow wary of him and jealous of him. It is said that a guardian’s task is only complete when the last obstacle is overcome and the last ward is safe.
Kent didn’t immediately take Li Hua away; he first scanned her.
[Name: Li Hua Dy Gondarius]
[Race: Human]
[Cultivation: None]
[Bloodline: Unknown]
[Physique: True Atomic Divine Body (Unawakened)]
-- This human has been blessed with the true body constitution of a divine. She possesses divinity and is destined to become a powerful Divine being.
-- But she also has a marker and seal placed on her body. This means she couldn’t cultivate even if she tried everything.
-- She can only live for the next 2 years if a cure is not found.
-- She also possesses a God-grade Spirit Root and a God-level immortal platform.
[Note: This information is only available because you are connected to her beyond normal means. The more your bond deepens with her, the more you will discover.]
<That’s all. What about the Cure Tower?>
Kent wasn’t angry yet. He wanted to keep it cool, considering the person everyone was trying to possess would die soon.
[The master doesn’t have to worry, as the cure will be made known once the Guardian Tower awakens. For now, the master has two years to become a grandmaster so the tower can awaken.]
<Great.> Kent sighed.
Kent gave Li Hua a stare. He pitied her in his heart, considering she had been born with a divine body, yet, because of that, she wouldn’t live long enough.
He couldn’t think of any reason why someone would place a marker on her or, more importantly, who knew she had a divine body and placed a marker on her.
Naturally, the moment the marker was erased, the person who placed the marker on her would be made known.
Perhaps that is what they wanted, considering they could have killed her instead of marking and sealing her. That doesn’t make sense.
But then again, perhaps they knew she wouldn’t amount to much, considering she couldn’t cultivate even if she tried.
But that was then. She has now met Kent, who would do anything as her Guardian to ensure her cure and safety from all harm.
Kent quickly lifted her onto his shoulder, but then he remembered the massacre outside, so he had to blindfold her for a minute. He wouldn’t want her to see the scene outside.
He was about to leave the cave when the tower prompted him.
[Master, there is someone else in here.]

chapters.title: Chapter 77: Jacob Ashland
paragraphs: Kent paused in his tracks as he heard the tower’s voice informing him there was another person inside the cave prison.
With his connection to Li Hua, he was able to pinpoint her location and even perform a vivid scan of the cave, but he sensed no one else.
If that was the case, did it mean his senses weren’t as strong as he thought? That was deeply unsettling. For a moment, Kent felt a creeping sense of vulnerability.
If his senses weren’t that good, wouldn’t he be in danger, especially if someone with exceptional concealing abilities came after him?
<Tower, how is this possible? I scanned the place but sensed no one aside from Li Hua.> Kent needed to understand before acting recklessly in the future.

[The master is indeed correct. However, the problem isn’t with the master—it lies with something deep underground in this cave. It possesses properties that interfere with the reality within a certain part of the cave.
The person is inside a cell that sits directly atop the treasure, so naturally, even a Root Great Sage wouldn’t be able to sense him.]
Kent raised an eyebrow. He set Li Hua down gently and whispered to her,
"Sit here and close your eyes. I’ll be back soon." He removed her blindfold and retrieved one of the banana cakes he had bought for her, placing it in her hands.
Li Hua nodded and obediently closed her cute, tiny eyes.
Kent smiled at how small and delicate she looked before turning to venture deeper into the cave.
<Tower, do you know what this treasure is made of or what it’s called?> Kent asked.
If there was a treasure capable of disrupting reality to this degree, he had to claim it. The only question was whether he had the means to do so.
Or, more importantly, did he even know what this treasure truly was?

[I can’t determine the true nature of this treasure, but I can calculate how deeply it is buried. That said, I will be able to identify the exact treasure once your soul reaches Tier 4 and your cultivation base enters the grandmaster stage.]
<Good to know.>
Kent retrieved his sword and moved forward. Soon, he stood in front of a cell where a young man he had met before was tied up with enchanted chains.

"What are you doing here?" Jacob Ashland, the son of Dave Ashland—who had once tried to challenge Kent to a death match because the woman he coveted had chosen another man—asked, fear evident in his eyes.
"I should be the one asking that. Isn’t this place your family’s torture house? What are you doing here, and in chains no less?" Kent asked, puzzled.
Jacob appraised him and sighed.
"I left the family, and because I know too much, my family wanted me dead. But the people who were supposed to kill me changed their minds and decided to sell me as a slave instead."
Jacob summarized everything, which left Kent even more puzzled. Still, he gave Jacob a thumbs up—at least he wasn’t entirely foolish and decided to leave the family destined to fall soon enough.

In truth, Jacob wasn’t as stupid as everyone thought him to be. He simply didn’t receive the same attention his elder sister did, primarily because of his average talent in cultivation. To his family, he was little more than a political tool to be used for their gain.
He was only meant to marry Lilian and then his family would take her from him and do to her what they wanted from the start.
So when he saw an opportunity, he took it and left. But he hadn’t anticipated his family coming after him, let alone wanting to kill him to silence him.
<Tower, should I kill him?> Kent had no problem killing him.
Leaving him alive held no meaning to him, considering he had already started making plans to destroy the Ashland Noble family for what they did to Li Hua and her grandma.
[The master may want to consider many things here.]
<Oh, do tell.>
[The master can consider bringing him to his side, where you can use him to learn more about the Ashland Noble family, which the master must destroy at all costs.]

Kent raised an eyebrow. It seemed the tower wanted them gone as well. Not surprising at all, considering the tower was meant to follow its master’s desires. It had to look for every opportunity that could help its master grow.
So, no matter the danger, as long as its master could handle it, it would use its powers to aid him. There is a saying: if everything is handed on a silver platter, one takes it for granted.
The more opportunities, the more quests to be given, which would all depend on how much stronger the master wanted to grow.
[That said, since the master doesn’t have a Slave Tower, the master can make him his servant, which would awaken the Servant Tower.]
<Servant Tower? How is that different from Slave?> Kent asked.
For some reason, he hated the idea of being a slave or having a slave. He might have joked about it with his master, but deep within, he detested the idea of having slaves or becoming anyone’s slave.

It was the last thing he had heard from the dark-cloth lady before he lost consciousness. Now, hearing he didn’t have a Slave Tower but a Servant Tower, he wanted to know the difference. He would rather kill Jacob or leave him than make him his slave.

[A slave doesn’t have free will, but a servant does. You wouldn’t be forcing him. However, the moment he becomes your servant, he won’t be able to betray you. But that also means you wouldn’t be able to kill him.
It’s a contract that will make you his master, but he can choose to reject the contract, in which case you wouldn’t be able to force him.]
<This sounds better, I think.>
Kent didn’t expect to have such an option. But at least, having him as his servant could prove valuable in the coming days. That said, the question remained.

Would he accept the proposal to become his servant? Bear in mind that Kent had already taken his dream woman from him, even if he was just being used as a pawn in a rather sinister game orchestrated by his father and his wife, Daisy.
The fact that he had lost the flower he so much craved should be enough reason to hate him for all eternity. But then again, Kent doesn’t need him as much as he needs him.
Kent didn’t truly need him, but he would be a great help if he was indeed going to take down a noble family. He would be a great help, indeed.
If only he knew this decision to add Jacob to his tower would one day prove to be one of the best decisions he had ever made. In fact, the benefits would start the moment he got his approval.
Kent looked at the chained individual and asked,
"Do you want to become my servant and serve me with all willingness?"

chapters.title: Chapter 78: First Servant, Krex-Nithal: The Undying Cockroach
paragraphs: Jacob lifted his head slowly, his face pale and battered from when the Dark Legion Guards picked him up from a brothel where he was planning to spend the rest of his meaningless life after leaving his family.
His eyes held a mix of anger, confusion, and something close to resignation. He didn’t speak at first, only stared at Kent as if trying to measure the sincerity behind his words.
He is angry, for one. But that was all: just anger.
Now, however, he heard something he never thought he would hear from the second most hateful person he had met.
Daisy Ashland is first by the way.
For a moment, there was silence. The weight of the question hung in the air, pressing on his rational mind. He could make a decision now that would change his life.
Finally, Jacob broke the silence.
"And if I refuse?" he asked, his voice hoarse but steady. He wasn’t about to act arrogant despite resolving himself to death days ago.
Yet death doesn’t want him, it seems.
Kent crossed his arms and tilted his head slightly. "Then I’ll release you," he said plainly. "You’ll be free to go wherever you want. I do not need someone unwilling to follow me."
Jacob’s eyes narrowed. "Why not just kill me, then? It would solve all your problems."
Kent gave a faint smirk. "I don’t have a reason to kill you. You’re not a threat to me, Jacob. But you could be an asset if you choose to be."
The words seemed to catch Jacob off guard. He blinked a few times, his shoulders slumping slightly as he processed the offer.
"You’ve already taken everything from me," Jacob said bitterly. "What’s left for me to serve you for?"
Kent’s expression hardened, his voice colder now.

"That’s up to you. You can keep clinging to your grudge and die with nothing, or you can find a new purpose. I’m offering you a chance to rise above what your family made you—a chance to stand for something real."

The prison fell silent again. Jacob’s hands clenched into fists, the chains around his wrists rattling softly. His breathing was uneven, but he held an expression that said he wasn’t stupid to do anything stupid.
"I’ll do it," he said at last.
Kent nodded a faint hint of approval in his eyes. "Good then. You won’t regret your decision."
When Kent responded to Jacobs’s declaration, the tower came to life.
[Requirement Met...Servant Tower Awakening]
[You have unlocked the Servant Tower. You must become a Root Grandmaster to awaken it fully]
[Servant Tower]
-- You can add people willing to serve you to your servant tower.
-- People added to the tower cannot betray you, nor can you betray them.
-- You will inherit a part of their soul strength as their trust in you grows.
-- You will earn a part of their spiritual Qi as they cultivate.
[Note: All other benefits will be added when you awaken the tower fully]
[You have added the first person to your servant tower. Name: Jacob Ashland. Trust Level: 12%]
[Your first servant has inherited a True name: Krex-Nithal (Locked)]
[First Servant: Jacob Ashland]
[Cultivation: Level 9 Root Master]
[True Name: Krex-Nithal]
< True Name: Krex-Nithal >
+ The Undying Cockroach +
-- In the Age of Ash, long before the rise of kingdoms, a humble insect survived the wrath of the Sunstorm, a divine calamity that scorched the land and extinguished all life it touched.
-- Legends speak of a cockroach that refused to die, crawling through fire, poison, and crushing darkness.
-- Curious about its defiance, the gods bound its essence into a True name—Krex-Nithal.
-- This name granted eternal resilience, embodying the insect’s undying spirit, and was whispered through the ages, coveted by warriors and immortals alike.
-- Those who wield it inherit the cockroach’s resilience, marking them as one who treads the line between life and death. They won’t die easily.
-- The Forgotten Codex records that Krex-Nithal was gifted to the first mortal hero who slew a chaos wyrm, surviving countless battles and becoming a legend, but his story ended mysteriously.
-- His body was never found, and it’s said the name now drifts in the void, seeking a worthy bearer.
<Tower, what is a ’True Name,’ and how does it make a difference?> Kent asked.
A True Name was something he was not familiar with. It looked good at a glance, but he felt he shouldn’t have known about it.

[A True Name is what binds one’s essence and being. A True Name is their life, and once it is proclaimed, one can take control over the person or beast. True Names are the person’s free will, in a way.
However, a True Name is also a person’s strength. Those with True Names are destined to grow and soar to the skies. True Names bestow special traits and aspects upon them.
In your first servant’s case, he had invoked the True Name of the undying legendary cockroach.
Of course, in your hands, it’s a blessing to them. You will know more when you fully awaken the tower. But to ease your emotions, knowing his True Name won’t make you his slave master.
Of course, you will have control over him, but in a good way.

The tower holds mysteries that will take you millennia to not even unravel the surface. So, for now, relax and let the various towers awaken before you make any decision on whether to invoke the name or not.
But you don’t have to worry, considering it’s locked. To unlock it, he would have to reach an 80% Trust level.]
<I see. Thanks, Tower.>
Kent calmed down a bit. He hated slavery, and knowing this, he felt like he was about to strip Jacob of his free will. But for now, he could only wait and learn more later.
Kent went on with the rest of the messages.
[You have unlocked a new skill; Fateful Servant]
[Skill Name: Fateful Servant]
[Grade: Divine]
[Rank: SSS]
[Effects: Passive]
-- Undying Will: Grants the servant immortality as long as their master lives. To a certain extent, they can die when under a powerful attack.
-- Enhanced Potential: Unlocks the servant’s latent abilities, exponentially boosting their growth and combat prowess.
-- Fate Link: The master can share senses, energy, and life force with the servant.
[Note: This skill taps into the Trust level of the master and the servant. The higher the trust level, the more powerful the effect of the skill]
’Tsk, from where I stand, this bastard has all the benefits. I only hope he becomes useful in the future.’ Kent chuckled inwardly but didn’t hate the turn of events.
First, he had earned a boost to his already robust soul strength. Now, he knew that regardless of the tower he awakened, he would gain a part of their soul strength, which, in a way, delighted him.
Second, he would gain some of his Spiritual Qi as he cultivated. One can say the tower is spoiling him rotten, But he knew better.
He now had Unity, Lilian, and Jacob as his Spiritual Qi banks. Since Li Hua had yet to reach the cultivation age, she couldn’t contribute.
But that was also fine. Kent could already see a future where he wouldn’t have to think about cultivating. All he would be doing was sleeping with women and growing strong.
Well, he was a dual cultivator, so in a way, he was cultivating even through sex. But he will also receive spiritual qi from those connected to him.

sentences.text: Jacob lifted his head slowly, his face pale and battered from when the Dark Legion Guards picked him up from a brothel where he was planning to spend the rest of his meaningless life after leaving his family.
His eyes held a mix of anger, confusion, and something close to resignation.
He didn’t speak at first, only stared at Kent as if trying to measure the sincerity behind his words.
He is angry, for one.
But that was all: just anger.
Now, however, he heard something he never thought he would hear from the second most hateful person he had met.
Daisy Ashland is first by the way.
For a moment, there was silence.
The weight of the question hung in the air, pressing on his rational mind.
He could make a decision now that would change his life.
Finally, Jacob broke the silence.
"And if I refuse?" he asked, his voice hoarse but steady.
He wasn’t about to act arrogant despite resolving himself to death days ago.
Yet death doesn’t want him, it seems.
Kent crossed his arms and tilted his head slightly.
"Then I’ll release you," he said plainly.
"You’ll be free to go wherever you want.
I do not need someone unwilling to follow me."
Jacob’s eyes narrowed.
"Why not just kill me, then?
It would solve all your problems."
Kent gave a faint smirk.
"I don’t have a reason to kill you.
You’re not a threat to me, Jacob.
But you could be an asset if you choose to be."
The words seemed to catch Jacob off guard.
He blinked a few times, his shoulders slumping slightly as he processed the offer.
"You’ve already taken everything from me," Jacob said bitterly.
"What’s left for me to serve you for?"
Kent’s expression hardened, his voice colder now.
"That’s up to you.
You can keep clinging to your grudge and die with nothing, or you can find a new purpose.
I’m offering you a chance to rise above what your family made you—a chance to stand for something real."
The prison fell silent again.
Jacob’s hands clenched into fists, the chains around his wrists rattling softly.
His breathing was uneven, but he held an expression that said he wasn’t stupid to do anything stupid.
"I’ll do it," he said at last.
Kent nodded a faint hint of approval in his eyes.
"Good then.

-- Curious about its defiance, the gods bound its essence into a True name—Krex-Nithal.
-- This name granted eternal resilience, embodying the insect’s undying spirit, and was whispered through the ages, coveted by warriors and immortals alike.
-- Those who wield it inherit the cockroach’s resilience, marking them as one who treads the line between life and death.
They won’t die easily.

<Tower, what is a ’True Name,’ and how does it make a difference?> Kent asked.
A True Name was something he was not familiar with.
It looked good at a glance, but he felt he shouldn’t have known about it.

chapters.title: Chapter 79: Back to The Mansion
paragraphs: Jacob stood in a daze, staring at Kent. For some reason, he could sense something had changed in him. However, he couldn’t quite pinpoint what it was.
Still, the feeling lingered—this was not the same Jacob his family had used as a pawn in their relentless hunger for power.
He had changed, and soon, his true nature—the one death seemed to forsake—would awaken. He would rise, serving his master with every fiber of his being.
"I’ll need your help in dealing with your family," Kent said, his tone calm.
"But for now, I don’t have a use for you. Take this, find somewhere in the city to relax, and use the time to reflect. Reevaluate your mindset and ask yourself if you truly want to follow me or not."
He paused. "Of course, you’ve already accepted becoming my servant, but that can change too. So, go and take this break. If I need your help, I’ll find you."
Kent tossed a storage pouch containing 30,000 spirit stones to his new servant, who, at that moment, trusted him no more than 12%.
Not that Kent cared much, though, in a strange way, he now cared enough. Somehow, he had triggered and bestowed a true name upon Jacob.
That alone meant Jacob would one day rise to the level of an undying warrior, akin to the undying cockroach Krex-Nithal, who defied the impossible odds stacked against it.
But it all depended on trust. If Jacob chose to linger at 12%, his destiny would remain shackled, stagnating as long as he refused to move forward.
Jacob accepted the pouch without a word, standing in silence for a few moments before turning and leaving.
As he passed Li Hua, he cast a curious glance at the small human Kent had rescued, his expression unreadable. Then, without a word, he stepped out of the cave.
But the moment he stepped outside, his breath hitched. Surrounding him were dozens of headless bodies, their lifeless forms scattered across the ground in a grotesque display of carnage.
He froze for a moment, his heart pounding. But that was just for a moment. Without any hesitation, he turned and bolted. The scene was too brutal, too overwhelming for him to bear.
[The Trust level of your First Servant Jacob Krex-Nithal has increased. Trust Level: 16%]
"I see," Kent murmured, a smirk tugging at the corner of his lips.
The sight outside had clearly left its mark on Jacob, nudging his trust upward. Not that Kent particularly cared about Jacob’s mental state at the moment.
After all, Jacob had yet to prove himself worthy of greater attention from his master. As a servant—but not a slave—his soul and mind were still his own, beyond the reach of Kent’s absolute command.
Kent picked Li Hua up, blindfolded her, and hoisted her onto his shoulder before walking out of the cave. He scanned the surroundings briefly, then decided to use his teleportation skill to move.
However, just as he was about to activate it, the tower’s voice interrupted him.
[Master, your Soul Cultivation has advanced to the 2nd Tier. You now possess sufficient soul strength to teleport back to the Alderford Mansion.
Currently, this ability can only be used once a week. However, as your soul strengthens, its frequency will increase.]
<I see. But won’t it affect Li Hua? We’re hundreds of miles away from the Alderford Mansion.>
[She will lose consciousness, but she won’t suffer any harm.]
<Alright. Do it.>
Kent issued the command. Almost instantly, a golden light enveloped him and Li Hua. A glowing spell circle appeared beneath them, and in the blink of an eye, they vanished.
A second later, they stood in his room at the mansion.
Before Kent could orient himself, Saintess Selene burst into the room, her sword drawn and her expression sharp.
"Kent... where have you been?" she demanded, her gaze locking onto him before flicking to the small human draped over his shoulder. Her brows shot up in surprise.
"Whatever you are thinking, Master, stop. I am not that kind of person." Kent lowered Li Hua, who had passed out, onto the bed and laid her down after removing her blindfold.
He then looked back at his master. "I like my women beautiful, legal, good with their hands, and overprotective." He walked closer to his master, only stopping when he was a foot away from her.
Saintess Selene’s heartbeat skipped for a moment when her gaze met Kent’s. For some reason, she could tell something had changed about him again, but at the moment, she wasn’t thinking about that.
No, her heart wasn’t allowing her to get curious. She focused on him for a whole minute before Kent broke the stare.
"Master, how hard is it to bring down a noble family? And when I say bring them down, I mean destroy them entirely." Kent spoke with eyes that suggested he was serious.
Saintess Selene’s mood also changed as she noticed the shift in the tone and expression of her disciple, whom she had only seen for a few hours now.
"What happened?" she asked.
Kent narrated everything, starting from when he first met Li Hua a few days ago. He told her about how he went looking for the small human, only to discover that someone was after her.
Then, he recounted finding Li Hua’s grandmother dead in the woods. Of course, he refrained from mentioning that he had become a soul cultivator and inherited the role of Li Hua’s Guardian.

He then detailed how he marched into Mokasa Prison and killed the guards as if chopping potatoes. Naturally, he exaggerated a bit about the events that transpired, but in the end, exaggeration or not, he did kill them.
When he reached the part where a peak Root Sage appeared, Saintess Selene’s expression changed.
However, Kent lied, saying he had used a life-saving artifact left by his shameless master to temporarily bring his strength to Root Saint, allowing him to defeat her.
The truth was that Kent himself didn’t know how he had killed the Dark Cloth lady. But he now has a way. He would find out in seven days since the tower had recorded everything.
"You really are something," Saintess Selene said with a smile after hearing about the adventures her disciple had experienced in just a few hours.
"Well, I don’t want to brag, but I am that awesome," Kent replied, puffing out his chest. Saintess Selene chuckled, but her expression soon grew serious.
"There are various ways to bring down a noble family, but none of them will be easy. That said, are you sure you want to do something like this?"

"I do. Although it’s just in name, I feel like a guardian to that small human, and I can’t live knowing some powerful people are watching her with dangerous intent and might put her life in danger at any moment," Kent replied.
Saintess Selene pondered for a while and sighed.
"You don’t have the strength to go after them. Noble families are not something you can handle at the moment. Many casualties would occur even with me and the Alderford Family joining you.
"That said, there is a way—but it would require you to become an important figure in this kingdom."
"Do tell, Master," Kent said.

chapters.title: Chapter 80: The Dark Devil Church
paragraphs: Myrathis, the human Continent, consists of four powerful kingdoms: Varyndor, Eldorath, Althea, and Kyrrith.
All these kingdoms are formidable; however, as in any empire, not all kingdoms possess equal strength. In this case, the Kyrrith Kingdom is the strongest of them all.
This is because Kyrrith specializes in warfare and weapon-making. Essentially, it is the major supplier of weapons and other warfare equipment throughout the continent.
Of course, this doesn’t mean they are supreme; the other three kingdoms are also powerful. If war were to break out, it wouldn’t result in a one-sided massacre.
However, while these powers are dominant on the continent, there are hidden forces that form the underworld chains.
These organizations operate in the shadows, concealing their involvement in the kingdoms’ affairs.
One such organization is the Dark Devil Church. They are a group of powerful egomaniacs who seek to create chaos wherever they go.
They care little for the effects their actions have on the four kingdoms as long as they can indulge in their pursuits and conduct their experiments.
The Dark Devil Church’s headquarters is located in the Twisting Vine Forest, just outside Stonefall City in the Kyrrith Kingdom.

The Twisting Vine is a place no sane person would dare to venture. Though there are no land or air monsters, everything about the forest is rooted in the ground. Yes... the trees themselves are the monsters.
It’s called the Twisting Vine because the moment you enter, you fall into the domain of a special kind of tree monster called the Twisting Lethal Vines.
Even a Root Great Sage wouldn’t dare to venture into its depths. Yet, somehow, the Dark Devil Church has established its headquarters there.
It is a tall, ominous building with stone walls as black as obsidian, exuding an eerie and dangerous aura. A group of masked figures in robes could be seen holding a meeting inside a large hall.
"Reports," a figure in a red robe commanded.

"My lord, I have reports from the Eldorath Kingdom," one of the dark-robed figures began. "The church has discovered a new spirit stone mine just outside Faywood City. However, the Faywood Noble family is making negotiations difficult."
"They are asking for 60% of the mine and 100 year-long contract. They also want us to assassinate the youngest son of King Lorian."

"Naturally, we haven’t reached any conclusion since killing the young prince will provoke war. However, that can be used to our advantage. My only worry now is the percentage they are asking for. I don’t know how to proceed, my lord."
The red-robed figure didn’t show any expression due to the mask on his face, but behind the mask, a frown appeared.
"This will indeed provoke a war, which we can weave into our plans. However, the percentage they are asking for is just too much."
"Find a way to get them to accept 50%. But if they don’t, you can always use the hard way. I am sure a few dark guards would love to have a field day with the women in the Faywood Noble family."

"I will heed your words, my lord." The dark-robed figure nodded. Behind the mask, he was smiling. Why? Because if they indeed chose to remain stubborn, he and his men would love to go on a rampage overnight.
"I bring reports from the Varyndor Kingdom." Another dark-robed figure, this time a woman, spoke.

"The Red Cyclone Sect and Winter Day Sect have been enslaved. Now, the two sects are under our command. This has given us more than enough specimens for the superhuman experiment. So far, the progress hasn’t exceeded 60%, but we are still working on it.

"With thousands of humans to choose from, we will be making progress soon. That aside, I also have to report that the Thornmarch and Oathfield Noble families have finally formed an alliance with us, and soon, others will join.
If we are lucky and more join, we will take over the kingdom in the next two years."

"Good work, Feyrite. I will be sure to assign adequate resources to your cause. That said, be sure to work faster on the superhuman project. We need it for our mega plan. Also, see if you can subdue the other sects.

"But don’t forget, never attempt to subdue the Thunderhoof Cavalry Sect. You can infiltrate to a certain stage but never attempt to subdue them. For now, we don’t have to create too much chaos we can’t handle.
"This goes for you all."
"Yes, my lord."
They all bowed.
"I bring reports from the Althea Kingdom," the next Dark figure said.

"The spirit root transplant project is moving steadily. So far, we have managed to acquire 30 Gold Grade, 8 Diamond Grade, and 2 Platinum spirit roots. We are also on track to acquire another Platinum Grade spirit root.

But that isn’t the main report. Recently, my subordinate located in Caprath City chanced upon a rare body constitution that hasn’t appeared for tens of thousands of years in the human world. I don’t know if any of you have heard of the infamous Atomic Divine Body."
"WHAT?"
The red-robed figure and the three other dark-robed figures exclaimed in a shocked tone.
"Are you telling us that the constitution, which, when it appeared outside the dwarven race can even cause gods to descend, has appeared in the Althea Kingdom?"
The red-robed figure asked in a commanding yet ecstatic tone.
"Yes, my lord. My subordinate is currently finding ways to secure her. She is capable, so I know for a fact she will secure her."

"Good. I will allow you to take three of the Dark Night Assassins to take charge of her training. We can’t let this slip through our fingers. In fact, cancel other projects for now and handle the Atomic Divine Body until I tell you otherwise," the red-robed figure said.
"I will heed your words, my lord." The face behind the mask of the dark-robed figure from Althea Kingdom was full of smiles and pride.
Of course, the other three held jealous looks behind their masks, too. Some even started having other thoughts.
"You’ve done a good job, Hyx," the red-robed figure said, sounding happy.
The reason was quite simple: the Dark Devil Church is more than it appears. It is on other continents and empires scattered throughout the world of Sonos.

Their main aim is to rule the entire world. If he were to make it known to the other Churches that he had acquired an Atomic Divine Body, they would become very jealous, and in fact, they would try to snatch her from him, which would provoke a war between them.
This, of course, is the ambitious plan of the red-robed figure. His ambitions are much bigger than the aim of the Dark Devil Church.
While they want to rule the world from different continents, his plan is much bigger. Because of that, he constantly seeks something that will give him an upper hand.
Having an Atomic Divine Body as your slave assassin would surely give him the upper hand he wants. He was determined to get his hands on her.
If only he knew that a very dangerous and angry Chaos Dragon had just become the guardian of the said Atomic Divine Body, he would have changed his mind and pursued other avenues.
The downfall of the church is imminent.

"The church has discovered a new spirit stone mine just outside Faywood City.
However, the Faywood Noble family is making negotiations difficult."
"They are asking for 60% of the mine and 100 year-long contract.
They also want us to assassinate the youngest son of King Lorian."
"Naturally, we haven’t reached any conclusion since killing the young prince will provoke war.
However, that can be used to our advantage.
My only worry now is the percentage they are asking for.
I don’t know how to proceed, my lord."
The red-robed figure didn’t show any expression due to the mask on his face, but behind the mask, a frown appeared.
"This will indeed provoke a war, which we can weave into our plans.
However, the percentage they are asking for is just too much."
"Find a way to get them to accept 50%.
But if they don’t, you can always use the hard way.
I am sure a few dark guards would love to have a field day with the women in the Faywood Noble family."
"I will heed your words, my lord." The dark-robed figure nodded.
Behind the mask, he was smiling.
Why?
Because if they indeed chose to remain stubborn, he and his men would love to go on a rampage overnight.
"I bring reports from the Varyndor Kingdom." Another dark-robed figure, this time a woman, spoke.
"The Red Cyclone Sect and Winter Day Sect have been enslaved.
Now, the two sects are under our command.
This has given us more than enough specimens for the superhuman experiment.
So far, the progress hasn’t exceeded 60%, but we are still working on it.
"With thousands of humans to choose from, we will be making progress soon.
That aside, I also have to report that the Thornmarch and Oathfield Noble families have finally formed an alliance with us, and soon, others will join.
If we are lucky and more join, we will take over the kingdom in the next two years."
"Good work, Feyrite.
I will be sure to assign adequate resources to your cause.
That said, be sure to work faster on the superhuman project.
We need it for our mega plan.
Also, see if you can subdue the other sects.
"But don’t forget, never attempt to subdue the Thunderhoof Cavalry Sect.
You can infiltrate to a certain stage but never attempt to subdue them.
For now, we don’t have to create too much chaos we can’t handle.
"This goes for you all."
"Yes, my lord."
They all bowed.
"I bring reports from the Althea Kingdom," the next Dark figure said.
"The spirit root transplant project is moving steadily.
So far, we have managed to acquire 30 Gold Grade, 8 Diamond Grade, and 2 Platinum spirit roots.
We are also on track to acquire another Platinum Grade spirit root.
But that isn’t the main report.
Recently, my subordinate located in Caprath City chanced upon a rare body constitution that hasn’t appeared for tens of thousands of years in the human world.
I don’t know if any of you have heard of the infamous Atomic Divine Body."
"WHAT?"
The red-robed figure and the three other dark-robed figures exclaimed in a shocked tone.
"Are you telling us that the constitution, which, when it appeared outside the dwarven race can even cause gods to descend, has appeared in the Althea Kingdom?"
The red-robed figure asked in a commanding yet ecstatic tone.
"Yes, my lord.
My subordinate is currently finding ways to secure her.
She is capable, so I know for a fact she will secure her."
"Good.
I will allow you to take three of the Dark Night Assassins to take charge of her training.
We can’t let this slip through our fingers.
In fact, cancel other projects for now and handle the Atomic Divine Body until I tell you otherwise," the red-robed figure said.
"I will heed your words, my lord." The face behind the mask of the dark-robed figure from Althea Kingdom was full of smiles and pride.
Of course, the other three held jealous looks behind their masks, too.
Some even started having other thoughts.
"You’ve done a good job, Hyx," the red-robed figure said, sounding happy.
The reason was quite simple: the Dark Devil Church is more than it appears.
It is on other continents and empires scattered throughout the world of Sonos.
Their main aim is to rule the entire world.

If he were to make it known to the other Churches that he had acquired an Atomic Divine Body, they would become very jealous, and in fact, they would try to snatch her from him, which would provoke a war between them.
This, of course, is the ambitious plan of the red-robed figure.
His ambitions are much bigger than the aim of the Dark Devil Church.
While they want to rule the world from different continents, his plan is much bigger.
Because of that, he constantly seeks something that will give him an upper hand.
Having an Atomic Divine Body as your slave assassin would surely give him the upper hand he wants.
He was determined to get his hands on her.
If only he knew that a very dangerous and angry Chaos Dragon had just become the guardian of the said Atomic Divine Body, he would have changed his mind and pursued other avenues.
The downfall of the church is imminent.

chapters.title: Chapter 81: Kent’s Decision
paragraphs: It’s been two days since Kent rescued Li Hua and returned her to the Alderford Mansion. He hadn’t gone to see his two vixens yet, nor had he taken the time to review the changes that had appeared in his body and the rewards from his quests.
Instead, he decided to learn from his master.
He learned a lot about how the world works and how best to handle the Ashland Noble Family. It was an informative discussion. In the end, Kent made two plans.
First, he would become a Pill Grandmaster (Grandmaster Alchemist) so he could start concocting Tier 3 to Tier 5 pills.
Those would give him the fame he was after. His master even supported his decision, partly because, for some reason, she didn’t want to share him with the Sect.

Yes, the woman didn’t know why, but she didn’t want Kent to get entangled with the academy on that level. Of course, if he joined the Alchemy Gate in the academy, he would gain power and fame, but also unnecessary enemies.
Another reason was that the Sect would try to suppress him when he rose above their current standards.
She had experienced how heavenly his pills were, and from that, she could tell Kent only needed a few years to break into the pill market with his perfect pills.
Of course, she would be there to protect him.

He was also strong, so she knew she wouldn’t have to do much. All she would need to do was focus on his sword training, and soon, if he remained consistent, he would become a Sword Grandmaster within months.
While the alchemy world may appear to be a rich market, the competition is also very tight and even dangerous. No alchemist would want to lose their value.
This was also the reason why no noble or merchant family would want to have any falling out with an alchemist. Of course, Kent’s plan revolved around this notion.
Once he gained fame, he would ensure the Ashland Noble Family became irrelevant while catapulting the Alderford Family to prominence. With his fame and riches, he could push the Ashland family out.
Then, the next phase—which he knew they would initiate—would take effect. No matter what, they would attack him, and he could use that as an excuse to retaliate and decimate them.
Kent wasn’t going to forgive them. Usually, he wouldn’t feel this vengeful, but after forming the guardianship bond with Li Hua, he felt like a shepherd who had nearly lost a sheep.
He wouldn’t stop until all threats around his ward/herd had been dealt with. That is the way of the guardian.
Aside from becoming a Grandmaster Alchemist, he wanted to hurry and break through to the Root Grandmaster stage.
Right now, his access to the tower is limited. Aside from just communicating with the tower and some minimal functions, everything else is locked away.
The Sword, Harem, Alchemy, Guardian, Soul Cultivation, and Servant Towers had all been locked away and would only be fully unlocked once he became a Grandmaster.
According to the tower itself, this has limited some things for him. So, Kent wants to hold back now and use the time to awaken the towers and see what they will bring him.
He is now safe because he has a Peak Root Sage as his master. So long as he is close to her, he wouldn’t have to worry about anything.
His only worry is how he would get a Pill Master to duel with so he can complete that requirement and become a Pill Grandmaster.
"Is she still not awake?" Saintess Selene asked immediately as Kent walked out of the room Li Hua had been sleeping in for the past two days.
"Yes, Master. I guess she needed the sleep from all the trauma of having witnessed her grandma’s death," Kent said as he sat down with a pondering expression.
"What is wrong?" Saintess Selene asked, watching Kent’s expression.
"Master, if I am not going to join the academy’s Alchemy Gate of the sect, how am I going to gain my alchemy badge?" Kent asked.

Joining the alchemy gate of the Divine Palace Sect would have won him a badge that he could use to gain some authority in the kingdom. But now that he wouldn’t be joining them, how then would he be able to gain the badge?

"You can participate in the upcoming Pill Master competition that will be held in the capital in four months. Although you don’t have a badge, you can participate and earn a badge by default, along with some cool rewards.
It will also be the best time to show off your skills to the entire kingdom."

"I see. But won’t that make me an even more hated target? I doubt the judges will even like a random kid taking their shine with his extremely flawless alchemy skills," Kent joked as he flashed a shameless grin at his master.
Saintess Selene shook her head as a smile appeared on her lips. Although she hadn’t known him for long, she didn’t hate his presence at all.
"You will be fine. After all, this competition happens every five years, and the Second Queen of the Kingdom oversees it, so I doubt anyone would misbehave.
But even so, I am here. Nobody will be stupid enough to come after you."
"Then I will rely on you, Master," Kent said, taking her hand. Saintess Selene looked at his behavior but brushed it to the back of her mind. Her heart, however, was beating like crazy.
"Now, about the Second Queen, what do you know about her?" Kent asked, looking deep into Saintess Selene’s eyes.
Her heartbeat slowed down for a moment. The whitish-purple eyes looking back at her were just too cute and innocent, yet their danger made her body turn hot.
"Pervert... I am not telling you anything." Saintess Selene tried to overcome the emotions that overwhelmed her.
She averted her gaze and chose not to continue the conversation. Kent just smiled, knowing she would be playing with his divine rod like a lollipop sooner rather than later.
She stood up and left the room to catch a fresh breath and evaluate her emotions. If possible, she would disown her disciple and run away. But then again, she couldn’t since she didn’t want to.
"In case you need a massage, don’t hesitate to ask, Master," Kent said, watching her quicken her steps and walk away.
"I will get you... You can keep playing hard to get all you want."
[A cat can only struggle for so long. Soon, the wolf will sink its fangs into it.]
"You know the drill, Tower, you know the drill," Kent smiled, hearing his no-good tower’s shameless comment.
Kent was particularly pleased with the kind of system he had received. So far, they had talked about many things, and he could tell that whoever created the tower was very visionary.

It was designed so he could get strong quickly but also work for the strength he would be gaining. Instead of the system dictating everything, he had free reign to do things as he saw fit. He and the tower would have to agree on the approach.
That was all he needed, and for that, he wanted to explore what there was to know about the tower.
"Tower, let’s review my progress so far and my rewards from the quests," Kent said, choosing to tackle that first before anything else.
[As you wish, Master.]
The tower began pulling up the details of his completed quests and his progress.

chapters.title: Chapter 82: The Enchanted Book
paragraphs: "Tower, before we get into the rewards, can you tell me more about the towers? I seem to have noticed that some were giving me classes and subclasses. What is the difference here?" Kent asked.

So far, he has unlocked the Harem, Alchemy, Swordsmanship, Soul Cultivation, Guardian, and Servant Towers. However, among these six towers, only three had given him a profession, so he just couldn’t wrap his mind around it.

[The towers are in two forms, Primordial and Mystical. Primordial Towers are designed to give you a class and subclasses once they are unlocked. The Swordsmanship, Alchemy, and Soul Cultivation Towers are examples of this.

Then there are the Mystical Towers, designed to aid the master in managing all the different aspects he wants to handle. For example, if you want to manage your women and ensure they grow along with you, the Harem Tower is designed for that.
Because you haven’t fully awakened the towers, you won’t understand much of what I am saying, but the moment you gain first-hand access to them, you will see how advanced and helpful they can be.
Just like how you have Dual Cultivation, you can exploit other avenues once you awaken it. The tower is more advanced than you think.]
"I see. So, how many Primordial and Mystical Towers are there?" Kent asked. Although he had no plans to awaken many, since focusing on all would be a headache, he still had to ask.

[This question cannot be answered as there are many towers to choose from. But since the master asked, I can say that if you meet the requirements, you will be able to unlock hundreds of towers. After all, you are the Master of the Towers.]
"That makes me happy to hear. It would be great, though, if I could bestow towers on my women and help them grow," Kent sighed.

"Alright, let’s dig in." Kent wasn’t about to focus on things he couldn’t access at the moment. Once he becomes a Tower Master by reaching the level of Root Grandmaster, he will be able to focus on that.
~[{Status Page}]~
Name: Kent
Age: 18
Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon
Class: Alchemist
SubClass: Swordsman | Soul Cultivation
Cultivation: Root Master - Lvl 5/9
Physical Strenght: 475
Physical Agility: 475
Physical Stamina: 505
Spiritual Strenght: 765
Mental Strength: 655
"It looks like the Soul Cultivation is contributing to my spiritual strength," Kent smiled, watching the status page.
So far, his stats had been boosted much higher, and although he didn’t know exactly how much he had grown, just feeling his soul strength, he could tell he had become much stronger.
"Tower, let’s continue with the Soul Cultivation subclass."
[Class Name: Soul Cultivator (Spirit Master)]
[Soul Essense: 2004]
[Level: Tier 2]
"This is good, then. Too bad I didn’t get any new skills besides [Soul Absorb]," Kent sighed.
So far, aside from having a powerful soul and the ability to absorb soul essence and memories, he didn’t have much use for the Soul Cultivation class.
[The master can buy Soul Cultivator skills and techniques from the Tower Store once it awakens.] The tower always had a fix. Kent could only nod to that.

"I guess I will focus on strengthening my soul so I can handle those techniques once I get them. That said, what next... Let’s focus on the quests for now. The Guardian and Servant Tower can be handled later."
[You have successfully completed a quest. Quest Name: Bounce that Ass]
[Rewards: Diary of the Celestial Alchemist Vol. 1]
"Wait, what? Tower, is this what I think it is?" Kent held a smile on his face. If this was what he was thinking, then he was about to become very happy.
[Yes, Master, this is exactly what you are thinking. The diary is an account of the Celestial Alchemist, the same alchemist you are learning from.]

"Damn, could my day get any better than this?" Kent smiled and retrieved the diary. It was a book like the small diaries back on Earth, just as he had expected. But this one was much more mystical in a way.
Just holding it gave Kent a sense of déjà vu. It felt so real to him in ways he didn’t understand. However, he was more than happy to be holding it.
He touched it against his forehead in an attempt to learn it quickly, but it didn’t disperse.
"Huh?"
[The master cannot use the same old way to learn this. This book is the account of the Celestial Alchemist. The master must read it like a good old book should be read.]
"I see." Kent wasn’t disappointed.
It had been a year since he had read like a normal person, so he could only start now. Of course, this diary was just around 70 pages, so he wouldn’t even need a week to finish it.
"Let me put this on hold for now. I suppose it contains additional knowledge on alchemy, and I cannot speed-read it like I used to."
Back on Earth, after he was killed, the police unearthed hundreds of books from his house, earning him the title God of Readers.
He had read hundreds of books, so after checking his online accounts and the reviews he had left, many authors were in tears.

Many had been searching for the reader named ’Xytor’ for years, never realizing their good old movie director was him. He made sure to correct them where they were wrong and encouraged them not to give up on their books.
It had been an emotional moment for many authors back on Earth.
"Next quest, Tower," Kent said with a smile. For some reason, he couldn’t wait to delve into the diary.
[You have successfully completed a quest. Quest Name: Guardian’s Arrogance]
[Rewards: Kingdom Building Enchanted Book]
"Another book. I wonder what this does." Kent retrieved the book, which was a little bigger than the diary. It was about the size of an A4 sheet and contained only one page.
"Tower!"
[Name: Kingdom Building Enchanted Book]
[Grade: Spiritual Grade]
[Type: Enchanted]

-- Long ago, the god of travelers sought to travel to a distant world. However, he knew nothing of this world, and from what he knew, you can’t ask for direction when you get there. Once you step in, you are on your own.
-- Nobody travels there. But the god of travelers wanted to go. So he sought out an enchantress, who he asked for a way to know everything about this world.

-- The enchantress created the [Kingdom Building Enchanted Book] and gave it to him. This book will tell him everything he needs to know about this strange world. In return, she asked for an unknown favor.
-- The God of Travelers readily accepted this unknown favor that was only made known when he bound with the book.
-- Till this day, the god of travelers never returned from his journey, and the enchantress never got the favor she asked for.
-- Nobody knew what this favor was and what happened to the god of travelers. But one thing is certain: whoever dares to bind with this book will inherit this favor.
-- The enchantress has willed it.
[Does the master wish to form a soul contract with this book]
